hits.title: [Kernel] Use FlashInfer CUDA BGMV MoE Kernel for Multi-LoRA MoE dispatch
hits.body:
Co-authored-by: Claude

## Purpose
This PR connects vLLM's MoE LoRA dispatch path to FlashInfer's BGMV MoE CUDA kernel (merged in https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3249). When FlashInfer with BGMV MoE support is installed, vLLM uses it via the `flashinfer.fused_moe` API. The Triton SGMV kernel remains as a fallback, selectable via environment variables.

This is the recommended integration path: kernel lives in FlashInfer, vLLM consumes it through the existing FlashInfer interface.

## Changes
* **flashinfer.py**: Add `has_flashinfer_bgmv_moe()` detection and lazy wrappers for `bgmv_moe_shrink` / `bgmv_moe_expand`
* **punica_gpu.py**:
  * Add CUDA/Triton backend selection via `VLLM_MOE_LORA_BACKEND` env vars (default: CUDA)
  * Add pre-allocated GPU buffer infrastructure (`_init_moe_bgmv_buffers`) for zero-allocation kernel calls
  * Add `add_lora_fused_moe_cuda` method that dispatches to FlashInfer's `bgmv_moe_shrink` / `bgmv_moe_expand`
  * Add cudagraph capture skip (MoE LoRA ops are not capture-safe)
  * Route `add_lora_fused_moe` between CUDA (FlashInfer) and Triton paths based on backend config
  * Add FP8->bf16 input cast in `add_lora_fused_moe` for FP8 quantized models (neither CUDA BGMV nor Triton MoE LoRA kernels support FP8 activations directly)
  * Add stream synchronization after expand to prevent race condition with shared buffer reuse across layers

## Related PRs
* https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40670 - Original PR with kernel implementation directly in vLLM (superseded by this approach)
* https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3249 - FlashInfer PR with the CUDA kernel (merged)

## Test Plan
Correctness verified by running vLLM's existing MoE LoRA kernel tests with FlashInfer dispatch enabled:
```
FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 VLLM_MOE_LORA_BACKEND=cuda \
  python -m pytest tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py -v
```

## Test Result
```
All 417 passed
```

Performance results are documented in the FlashInfer PR (https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3249) and the original vLLM PR (#40670).

hits.title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Keep activations MXFP8 between DeepGEMM kernels
hits.body:
## Purpose

DeepGEMM's DeepSeek-V4.1 kernels can hand FP8 activations to each other, but vLLM re-quantized their BF16 outputs before every dense projection: 127 standalone MXFP8 quantize launches per decode step at C1 (TP4), plus the quantize half of the Mega-MoE input staging. This PR wires the FP8 outputs DeepGEMM already provides to the consumers, and runs those consumers on DeepGEMM.

One decoder layer, decode step. `[q]` = standalone MXFP8 quantize launch, `sf` = the UE8M0 group scales.

**Before** — every DeepGEMM kernel returns BF16, and a FlashInfer quantize kernel re-creates MXFP8 before each consumer:

```
attention sublayer
  mega_mhc (post+pre+RMSNorm) ──bf16──┬──▶ compressor score / indexer weights GEMMs (bf16, unchanged)
                                      └──▶ [q] ──mxfp8+sf──▶ FlashInfer GEMM  fused_wqa_wkv
  attention ──▶ fp8_einsum wo_a ──bf16──▶ [q] ──mxfp8+sf──▶ FlashInfer GEMM  wo_b ──▶ reduce-scatter

FFN sublayer
  mega_mhc (post+pre+RMSNorm) ──bf16──┬──▶ router gate + top-k (bf16, unchanged)
                                      └──▶ prepare_megamoe = [q] into symm buffer + pack top-k ──▶ fp8_fp4_mega_moe
```

**After** — the producers emit MXFP8 with packed scales directly, the consumers run on DeepGEMM `fp8_gemm_nt`:

```
attention sublayer
  mega_mhc ──bf16──────────────────────▶ compressor score / indexer weights GEMMs (unchanged)
           ──mxfp8+sf (y_fp8, y_gemm_sf)─▶ DeepGEMM GEMM  fused_wqa_wkv        (not under SP: input is all-gathered in bf16)
  attention ──▶ fp8_einsum wo_a ──mxfp8+sf ((z, sf) output)──▶ DeepGEMM GEMM  wo_b ──▶ reduce-scatter

FFN sublayer
  mega_mhc ──bf16─────────────────────────────────────▶ router gate + top-k (unchanged)
           ──mxfp8+sf written straight into the symm buffer (y_fp8, y_routed_sf, y_shared_sf)
                                                       ──▶ prepare_megamoe = pack top-k only ──▶ fp8_fp4_mega_moe
```

| per layer | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| standalone quantize launches | 3 (+ the quantize half of `prepare_megamoe`) | 1 under SP (`fused_wqa_wkv`), 0 otherwise |
| dense GEMM kernel | FlashInfer CuTe-DSL ×2 | DeepGEMM `fp8_gemm_nt` (1,1,32) ×2 |
| bytes between mHC / einsum and their consumers | bf16 out + fp8 in | fp8 out only |

Pieces:
- `DeepGemmMxfp8LinearKernel` (2D `fp8_gemm_nt`, recipe (1,1,32)); its activations carry a new `QuantKey` `kMxfp8DynamicDeepGemm` (int32 packed UE8M0 scales) so a FlashInfer-layout producer can never be routed to a DeepGEMM consumer or vice versa. The model marks `wo_b` / `fused_wqa_wkv` with `deep_gemm_activations`, and ModelOpt's post-load selects the kernel for them the same way it does for `is_bmm` layers.
- `mega_mhc` wrapper: optional `y_fp8`/`y_gemm_sf` and `y_fp8`/`y_routed_sf`/`y_shared_sf` outputs (DeepGEMM already implements them), reported as a typed `MegaMhcFp8Outputs`; the MoE leg is passed explicitly (`DeepseekV4MoE.forward(staged=...)` → `experts.forward_staged`) and `stage_megamoe_routing` repacks only the top-k.
- `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj(fp8_z=True)`: `fp8_einsum` emits `(z, sf)`; also in the mega-attention backend's `_o_proj`.
- Under sequence parallel the attention input is all-gathered in BF16 after the norm, so `fused_wqa_wkv` stays on FlashInfer there (FP8 all-gather is follow-up work).
- The new `fp8_gemm_nt` variants are pre-compiled by the existing DeepGEMM startup warmup (layers found through the `deep_gemm_warmup_provider` protocol).
- Binds wherever SM100 + DeepGEMM are available (checked at construction; other platforms keep their kernels with a logged reason). No new flag.

Duplicate check: searched open PRs for `mega_mhc y_fp8`, `y_gemm_sf`, `fp8_einsum`, `DeepGemmMxfp8LinearKernel`, `prepare_megamoe_inputs`, `wo_b quantize`, and by touched file. #57679 (restores the `wq_b` query-quant fusion) is complementary and untouched here; #56751 (skinny GEMM, M ≤ 4) quantizes in-kernel for the same projections at tiny M, a separate mechanism; #55505 (input-scale contract) does not conflict.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/test_dsv41_deepgemm_fp8_chain.py   # SM100
```
```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 64
```
Baseline: the same command on main. `vllm bench serve` random 4096/256, ignore-eos, one server at a time; GSM8K via lm-eval 0.4.12 (5-shot chat, thinking off, greedy, 1319 questions).

## Test Result

4×B200, TP4 + EP4, MegaMoE + SP, FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV.

- Unit tests: 21 passed (DeepGEMM kernel vs FlashInfer CuTe-DSL at M ∈ {1,4,7,64,300}; pre-quantized input bit-identical to in-kernel quant; `mega_mhc` FP8 outputs bit-exact MXFP8 of its BF16 output, MoE layout bit-identical to `prepare_megamoe_inputs`; einsum FP8 output vs quantized BF16 output; routing-only staging).
- Greedy outputs identical on 8/8 prompts × 64 tokens.
- C1 decode step (torch profiler, 61 steps): GPU busy 7.64 → 6.85 ms (−10 %), quantize launches 130 → 90.

| lane | baseline | PR | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| C1 ×3 TPOT | 6.58 / 6.58 / 6.58 ms | 6.50 / 6.50 / 6.50 ms | −1.2 % |
| C4 ×2 tok/s (TPOT) | 517 / 520 (6.97 / 6.94 ms) | 531 / 530 (6.83 / 6.86 ms) | +2.4 % (−1.6 %) |
| C4 ×2 TTFT | 201 / 199 ms | 184 / 183 ms | −8 % |
| C16 ×3 tok/s (TPOT) | 1347 / 1346 / 1340 (9.92 / 9.88 / 10.03 ms) | 1365 / 1357 / 1368 (9.85 / 9.86 / 9.73 ms) | +1.5 % (−1.3 %) |
| C64 ×1 tok/s (TTFT) | 1848 (2360 ms) | 1880 (2124 ms) | +1.7 % (−10 %) |
| GSM8K flexible / strict | 0.9621–0.9659 / 0.7817–0.7832 (3 baselines) | 0.9644 / 0.7877 | unchanged |

After the plumbing refactor (kernel selection through ModelOpt post-load, typed mHC outputs, explicit staged MoE input): 21 unit tests pass, C1 TPOT 6.50 / 6.50 / 6.50 ms, GSM8K 0.9636 / 0.7915, greedy outputs coherent on 12 prompts.

At C1 the host loop (~6.5 ms/step) bounds TPOT, so most of the GPU saving shows from C4 up. The FP8-output `mega_mhc` variants JIT-compile on first use per prefill shape, like the BF16 variants today (cache persists under `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR`).

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); the human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the measurements.

hits.title: [Model][Experimental] DeepSeek V4 w4a4 MegaMoE support
hits.body:
seealso: #42845 https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/issues/338
## Purpose

MegaMoE currently packs activations as FP8 (E4M3) in the symmetric buffer before dispatch. On Blackwell (SM100), FP4 (E2M1) packing would halve the buffer footprint and unlock the MXF4 mainloop (K=64 dense vs K=32 padded) in DeepGEMM.

However, upstream DeepGEMM does not yet support FP4 activations end-to-end. The `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` kernel hardcodes `a_dtype_t = float_e4m3_t`, `get_symm_buffer_size_for_mega_moe` allocates input token buffers at FP8 width (`hidden` bytes/token), and the dispatch stage TMA loads assume FP8 layout. The `use_fp8_dispatch` parameter exists in the API signature but is not wired through to the buffer sizing or kernel logic. An RFC has been filed at deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM to track this.

This PR provides a **proof-of-concept** using `sgl-deep-gemm>=0.1.0`, which ships a `mega_moe_pre_dispatch()` CUDA kernel that handles E2M1 packing + FP4-aware buffer allocation. Two opt-in env vars, both default off:
- `VLLM_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_FP4_ACTS` -- use `deep_gemm.mega_moe_pre_dispatch()` for E2M1 activation packing instead of the Triton staging kernel
- `VLLM_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_MXF4_KIND` -- switches to `kind::mxf4` mainloop, requires FP4 acts

When enabled, imports external `deep_gemm` for buffer allocation and pre-dispatch. When disabled, vendored `vllm.third_party.deep_gemm` is used as before -- zero change to default path.

Flags forwarded to the external deep_gemm via `os.environ.setdefault("DG_USE_FP4_ACTS", ...)` so explicit `DG_USE_*` overrides still win.

Files: `vllm/envs.py`, `vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v4.py`

## Upstream Gap Analysis

Checked deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM (latest, identical to vendored commit 891d57b for the mega module):

- `csrc/apis/mega.hpp`: `get_symm_buffer_size_for_mega_moe` accepts `use_fp8_dispatch` but ignores it -- `input_token_buffer` is always `layout::Data(hidden)` (FP8, 1 byte/element)
- `sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe.cuh` line 162-163: `a_dtype_t = cutlass::float_e4m3_t` -- UMMA configured for FP8 activations only
- Dispatch pull stage: TMA loads `kHidden` bytes per token (FP8 width)
- `slice_input_buffers` returns `x` as `[tokens, hidden]` float8, `x_sf` as `[tokens, hidden/128]`

None of these support FP4 activations. Full FP4 activation support requires changes at the C++/CUDA kernel level (buffer sizing, TMA load widths, UMMA A-matrix dtype), which is being tracked via the upstream RFC.

## Test Plan

Hardware: 8x B200 (SM100, 183GB). Accuracy: GSM8K full test set (1319 samples), greedy decoding, max_tokens=2048, concurrency=32.

Dep: `pip install sgl-deep-gemm==0.1.0`

V4-Flash (256 experts, hidden=4096, 43 layers), DP=4:

```bash
# w4a8 baseline
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --data-parallel-size 4 \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --enforce-eager

# w4a4 (this PR)
VLLM_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_FP4_ACTS=1 VLLM_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_MXF4_KIND=1 \
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --data-parallel-size 4 \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --enforce-eager
```

V4-Pro (384 experts, hidden=7168, 61 layers), TP=8:

```bash
# w4a8 baseline
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --enforce-eager

# w4a4 (this PR)
VLLM_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_FP4_ACTS=1 VLLM_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_MXF4_KIND=1 \
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --enforce-eager
```

Eval: hit `/v1/chat/completions`, extract final number after `####`, compare against reference.

## Test Result

### Accuracy (GSM8K, 1319 samples, greedy)

V4-Flash: w4a8 93.86% (1238/1319) -> w4a4 94.39% (1245/1319), delta +0.53%
V4-Pro: w4a8 91.81% (1211/1319) -> w4a4 91.13% (1202/1319), delta -0.68%

Both within noise. No meaningful accuracy degradation from FP4 activation packing.

### Performance (V4-Flash, DP=4, 8×B200)

Benchmark config: 500 prompts, input_len=1024, output_len=8, max-concurrency=64, request-rate=inf, `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 512`, random dataset.

| Metric | w4a8 | w4a4 | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Request throughput (req/s) | 11.21 | 17.73 | **+58.2%** |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 11,565.65 | 18,294.09 | **+58.2%** |
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 89.66 | 141.81 | **+58.2%** |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 3,789.39 | 1,834.52 | **-51.6%** |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 832.51 | 639.82 | **-23.1%** |
| P99 TTFT (ms) | 12,302.93 | 12,063.23 | -1.9% |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 272.46 | 251.78 | **-7.6%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 75.91 | 69.89 | **-7.9%** |

Key takeaway: ~58% throughput improvement, ~52% mean TTFT reduction. The gain is dominated by prefill (MXF4 mainloop K=64 dense vs K=32 padded). Decode TPOT improves ~8% from reduced buffer bandwidth.

## What Happens When Upstream Supports FP4 Acts

Once deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM wires `use_fp8_dispatch=False` through to buffer sizing + kernel:
1. Bump vendored commit in `cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake`
2. Replace `sgl-deep-gemm` path with a Triton FP4 staging kernel (~40 lines, E2M1 bucketize + pack) or use whatever staging API upstream provides
3. Change `get_symm_buffer_for_mega_moe(..., use_fp8_dispatch=False)` -- the parameter already exists
4. Remove import branches (3 sites), drop `sgl-deep-gemm` dep
5. `DG_USE_FP4_ACTS` / `DG_USE_MXF4_KIND` env forwarding likely becomes unnecessary -- remove `_apply_mega_moe_dg_env`
6. Move env vars from experimental to stable

---

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

hits.title: [Perf] Warm up DeepGEMM MegaMoE kernels before serving
hits.body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution -->
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The DeepGEMM warmup covers `fp8_gemm_nt` and the grouped MoE GEMM. It does not cover `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` or the `bf16_mega_gate` that routes into it. With `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi K3 therefore JIT-compile these kernels on the first request at each new prefill size. This PR adds them to `deep_gemm_warmup.py`, following the structure of the two existing DeepGEMM warmups there.

## Claims

- No serving-time compiles of the MegaMoE kernels: `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, `bf16_mega_gate` and the Triton input-staging kernel. Before: 60 DeepGEMM compiles in one DeepSeek-V4 benchmark run. For Kimi K3, the 2 SiTU `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` compiles during serving that cost 2.6-2.9 s of TTFT each go to 0, at about +10 s of startup.
- MTP speculative decoding needs nothing extra. The DeepSeek-V4 MTP drafter's MegaMoE layer uses the same kernels as the target's, and there were 0 DeepGEMM compiles during serving with MTP on.
- DeepSeek-V4: the first request at a new prefill size no longer stalls for 3.5 to 6 s. It now takes about the same time as a repeat. The exception is a one-time 60-85 ms communication-buffer setup on the server's first large prefill, which is not a compile (see Details).
- Cost: for DeepSeek-V4, the first startup on a cold DeepGEMM cache takes about 4 to 5 min longer (+247 to +299 s on fully empty caches). A warm restart takes the same time as before. For Kimi K3, it is about +10 s.

## Validation

**Setup (DeepSeek-V4).** DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 2x B300, TP2 + EP2, `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, `max_num_batched_tokens` 16384, `--max-model-len 16384`, prefix caching off, Model Runner V2. vLLM precompiled wheel `3ca00a82` (cu130) with its bundled DeepGEMM.

Each run used a fresh `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` seeded with every non-mega DeepGEMM kernel, so only the mega kernels start cold.

**Workload.** One request at a time: token-ID prompts to `/v1/completions`, `max_tokens` 4, streamed time to first token (TTFT).
1. Six fixed lengths (100 to 8000 tokens). Each gets a first request, then 3 repeats with new random tokens.
2. 40 seeded random lengths from 51 to 15504 tokens. The warmup did not pick these.
3. 32 concurrent requests.

**JIT compiles during serving.** Counted as new entries in the DeepGEMM cache dir between "Application startup complete" and the end of the workload, across all kernel families. Triton, CuTeDSL and TileLang compiles were counted with `--jit-monitor-verbose`.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `sm100_bf16_mega_gate` | 58 | 0 |
| `sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe` | 2 | 0 |
| other DeepGEMM families | 0 | 0 |
| Triton `_prepare_megamoe_inputs_kernel` | ≥1 (see note) | 0 |

On main, the Triton row comes from the default (non-verbose) JIT monitor, which logs only the first compile per kernel, so the true count is unknown. The previous revision of this PR, which warmed without a padding mask, compiled 3 variants for just three prompt lengths in a verbose run.

A separate single-GPU check called both kernels for every per-rank token count from 1 to 8192 after the warmup's representative sizes. It produced 0 new cache entries. An independent rerun of the patched server, with 20 prompt lengths, 16 of them chosen to give unaligned per-rank chunks, saw 0 JIT events.

**TTFT, first request vs median of 3 repeats (ms):**

| prompt tokens | main, first | main, repeat | this PR, first | this PR, repeat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 |
| 2000 | 3503 | 106 | 112 | 103 |
| 4000 | 5913 | 119 | 178 | 117 |
| 8000 | 3489 | 136 | 141 | 136 |

- 40 random lengths: 24 of the 40 requests on main took 3.5 to 6.0 s. The slowest on this PR took 0.27 s. Total TTFT went from 90.1 s to 6.1 s.
- 32 concurrent requests: worst TTFT went from 8.33 s to 1.47 s.

**Startup, `init engine` (profile, KV cache, warmup, graph capture):**

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| cold mega-kernel cache (all other kernels cached) | 141 s | 428 s |
| fully empty caches, no MTP (separate tester run) | 444 s | 691 s (+247 s) |
| fully empty caches, with MTP (separate tester run) | 406 s | 705 s (+299 s) |
| warm restart, same cache dir | 63 s | 63 s |

KV cache sizing is unchanged: 163.13 GiB and 465,145 tokens in both.

**MTP (DeepSeek-V4, `--speculative_config.method=mtp --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens=2`, same setup and workload):**

| MegaMoE compiles during serving | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| seeded cache (mega kernels cold), 1 run | not run | 0 |
| fully empty caches, 1 run (separate tester) | 2 `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, 10 `bf16_mega_gate`, 6 Triton staging | 0 |

On this PR's commit with MTP: the server was healthy, GSM8K (200 questions, 5-shot) scored 0.970, and mean MTP acceptance length was 2.62 on GSM8K. On the random-token benchmark, acceptance was 1.61, against 1.55 on the previous revision. DeepGEMM compiles during serving: 0.

The drafter needs no extra warmup. Its MegaMoE layer reuses the target's kernels, and the tester's tracer saw no DeepGEMM compile in the drafter during serving on either build.

**Kimi K3 (`mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75`, a pruned checkpoint):** 4x B300, TP4 + EP4 with sequence parallelism, `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192 (2048 per rank), fp8 KV, no prefix caching, no spec decode.
- Each run started with empty DeepGEMM, Triton, Inductor and vLLM caches. One run per build.
- Workload: one 3000-token request, a second 3000-token request with new tokens, then 137, 1500, 5000 and 8000 tokens.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| DeepGEMM compiles during serving | 2 (`fp8_fp4_mega_moe` SiTU, `block_m` 128 and 192) | 0 |
| Triton `_prepare_megamoe_inputs_kernel` compiled during serving | yes (ranks 1-3, first request) | no |
| TTFT at 1500 / 5000 tokens | 2734 / 3139 ms | 153 / 244 ms |
| `init engine` | 46 s* | 56-57 s |

\*The main run had a warm FlashInfer JIT cache from an earlier run. The PR runs had one too, so the +10 s compares like with like.

On both builds, two non-MegaMoE kernels still compile during serving: the Inductor kernel `triton_poi_fused_mul_sigmoid_0`, on the first prefill above the capture sizes, and the KDA gated RMSNorm Triton kernel `layer_norm_gated_fwd_kernel`. They are outside this PR.

**Fully cold cache.** With every DeepGEMM and Triton cache empty (not just the mega kernels), three other DeepGEMM kernel families still compile on first use with this PR. They are outside MegaMoE and left for follow-ups:
- `fp8_einsum` in `o_proj` (`sm100_fp8_gemm_1d1d`): 2 kernels.
- `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`: 8 kernels without MTP, 6 with MTP.
- The sparse indexer's `sm100_mqa_logits`: 1 kernel.

With MTP, the spec-decode rejection-sampler Triton kernels also compile on first use on both builds. That is unrelated to this PR.

**Tests.** `tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py` adds two CPU tests:
- The layer predicate is False for other models, and neither model module is imported. It is True only for DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi K3 MegaMoE layers.
- The warmup sizes for each `bf16_mega_gate` config are above the gate's token threshold, so the forward reaches the kernel.

All 8 tests pass.

**CI gap.** This path needs SM100 GPUs, DeepSeek-V4 or Kimi K3 with the native MegaMoE backend, and expert parallelism. CI has no such setup, so the validation above was run by hand.

<details>
<summary>Repro commands</summary>

```bash
# server (baseline: same command on main)
export VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=<fresh dir>
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=mxfp4 \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --jit-monitor-verbose --port 8234

# client: fixed lengths x (1 first + 3 repeats), 40 random lengths, 32-request burst;
# records TTFT and the new DeepGEMM cache entries per request
SWEEP=40 python bench.py 8234 $DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR results.json
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>bench.py</summary>

```python
"""First-hit benchmark. Phase 1 (fixed): for each prompt length, one request
at a time: a first hit, then REPEATS more with fresh random tokens. Phase 2
(sweep, optional): random lengths the warmup did not pick, then a concurrent
burst (mixed prefill + decode). Records TTFT and every DeepGEMM JIT cache
entry created during serving, per kernel family."""
import collections, concurrent.futures as cf, json, os, random, re, sys, time
import requests

port, dgdir, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
LENGTHS = [int(x) for x in os.environ.get("LENGTHS", "100,400,1000,2000,4000,8000").split(",")]
REPEATS = int(os.environ.get("REPEATS", "3"))
SWEEP = int(os.environ.get("SWEEP", "0"))
URL = f"http://localhost:{port}/v1/completions"
MODEL = "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash"
cache = os.path.join(dgdir, "cache")

def entries():
    return set(os.listdir(cache))

def family(e):
    m = re.match(r"(?:kernel\.)?(.+?)\.[0-9a-f]{32}$", e)
    return m.group(1) if m else e

def fam_count(es):
    return dict(collections.Counter(family(e) for e in es))

def ttft(prompt_ids, max_tokens=4):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    r = requests.post(URL, json=dict(model=MODEL, prompt=prompt_ids, max_tokens=max_tokens,
                                     temperature=0, stream=True, ignore_eos=True),
                      stream=True, timeout=3600)
    first = None
    for line in r.iter_lines():
        if line and line.startswith(b"data: ") and line != b"data: [DONE]" and first is None:
            first = time.perf_counter() - t0
    return first, time.perf_counter() - t0

rng = random.Random(0)
def prompt(L):
    return [rng.randrange(1000, 100000) for _ in range(L)]

start = entries()
print(f"entries at ready: {len(start)} {fam_count(start)}", flush=True)
rows = []
ttft(prompt(8))  # HTTP/tokenizer warm; 4 per-rank tokens -> no mega gate
for L in LENGTHS:
    for i in range(1 + REPEATS):
        before = entries()
        t, e2e = ttft(prompt(L))
        new = entries() - before
        rows.append(dict(phase="fixed", prompt_len=L, rep="first" if i == 0 else f"repeat{i}",
                         ttft_s=t, e2e_s=e2e, new=fam_count(new)))
        print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
after_fixed = entries()
sweep_lengths = []
if SWEEP:
    srng = random.Random(1)
    sweep_lengths = sorted(srng.randrange(17, 16380) for _ in range(SWEEP))
    for L in sweep_lengths:
        before = entries()
        t, e2e = ttft(prompt(L))
        rows.append(dict(phase="sweep", prompt_len=L, rep="first", ttft_s=t, e2e_s=e2e,
                         new=fam_count(entries() - before)))
        print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
    # concurrent burst: 32 requests, mixed lengths, 64 output tokens -> prefill + decode mix
    burst = [prompt(srng.randrange(17, 6000)) for _ in range(32)]
    before = entries(); t0 = time.perf_counter()
    with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(32) as ex:
        res = list(ex.map(lambda p: ttft(p, 64), burst))
    rows.append(dict(phase="burst", prompt_len=-1, rep="32 concurrent", ttft_s=max(r[0] for r in res),
                     e2e_s=time.perf_counter() - t0, new=fam_count(entries() - before)))
    print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
end = entries()
summary = dict(rows=rows, entries_at_ready=fam_count(start), new_during_fixed=fam_count(after_fixed - start),
               new_during_serving=fam_count(end - start), new_entries=sorted(end - start),
               sweep_lengths=sweep_lengths)
json.dump(summary, open(out, "w"), indent=1)
print("new during serving:", summary["new_during_serving"])
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** Both kernels choose a JIT config from the per-rank token count:
- `bf16_mega_gate`: block tokens, MMA CTAs, split-K, expert groups and stages (`heuristics/mega_gate.hpp`). That is 87 configs for per-rank sizes 17 to 8192.
- `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`: `block_m` in {16, 32, 64, 128, 192, 240}.

Startup only compiles the sizes that the profile run and CUDA graph capture hit, here 512 or fewer tokens per rank. Every other prefill size compiles on first use, about 1.7 s per kernel. DeepSeek-V4 needs two gate kernels per size, because hash-routed and bias-routed layers pass different optional inputs.

**Design.** The warmup lives in `deep_gemm_warmup.py`, with the same parts as the existing DeepGEMM warmups:
- A layer predicate that matches DeepSeek-V4's `DeepseekV4MoE` and Kimi K3's `KimiMoE` when they use the native MegaMoE backend.
- A cache constant.
- `_get_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_m_values`: for every per-rank size, it asks DeepGEMM for the `block_m` and, for DeepSeek-V4, the gate config. It keeps the largest size of each distinct config (95 sizes for DeepSeek-V4 here), because DeepSeek-V4 only calls `bf16_mega_gate` above a small token threshold and a config's largest size is always above it. The configs come from DeepGEMM's own getters, so the dedup is exact and `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=full` would add nothing.
  - Kimi K3 routes with its `GateLinear`, which the bf16x3 router warmup already covers, so for Kimi only `block_m` matters.
  - Kimi's experts call the SiTU variant of `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, which picks `block_m` with the same heuristic.
- A private worker and a public loop, an `elif` branch in `_count_warmup_iterations`, and calls in `deep_gemm_warmup`.

The worker runs the whole MoE layer at each size, not the raw kernels:
- The gate gets the same optional inputs it gets in serving.
- Every EP rank runs the same sizes in the same order, which the collective MegaMoE kernel needs.
- It runs under a minimal forward context with a padding mask, because the layer reads `is_padding` from the forward context. This makes the Triton input-staging kernel compile the variants serving uses.
- Under sequence parallelism with `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` on (the default), ranks above 0 get mask slices at any alignment, so each size runs once with an aligned slice and once with an unaligned one.

The predicate looks the model modules up in `sys.modules`, as other model-specific warmups in this package do (`kimi_k3_triton_warmup.py`, `qwen4_exp_qsa_warmup.py`), so other models import neither model. The cache key reads two DeepSeek-V4-only attributes (`tid2eid`, `image_sentinel_lo`) with `getattr`, because they do not exist on Kimi K3. The two config getters are reached through `_import_deep_gemm`, as in the model code.

`models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py` gains one line, which stores `use_sequence_parallel` on `KimiMoE` as `DeepseekV4MoE` already does. The warmup needs it to compute the per-rank token count.

<details>
<summary>Startup trade-off: where the cold warmup time goes</summary>

- About 84% of the cold warmup is serial `nvcc` time for 136 gate kernels (1.7 s each).
- About 14% is about 24 Triton staging variants.
- About 3% is 3 MegaMoE kernels.
- The layer forwards and the size search take under 1 s.

Compiling in parallel threads crashed inside DeepGEMM's JIT, which has no locking and no compile-only API. Parallel compilation would need DeepGEMM changes. vLLM keeps the DeepGEMM cache in `~/.cache/vllm/deep_gemm`, so the cold cost is paid once per machine and DeepGEMM version.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Remaining one-time first-request cost</summary>

The first eager prefill whose reduce-scatter falls in the MNNVL multimem size range sets up a symmetric-memory buffer (`_init_mnnvl_multimem_reduce_scatter_buffer`). This adds 60-85 ms to that one request (+61, +66 and +83 ms in three runs). CUDA graph capture skips this setup. It is paid once per server and is not a compile. A torch profile and a request-order test confirm both points.
</details>

**Limitations.** DeepSeek-V4 was validated only on 2x B300 with TP2 + EP2 and Model Runner V2, with and without MTP. Kimi K3 was validated only with a pruned checkpoint on 4x B300, TP4 + EP4, Model Runner V2.
- Not run: Model Runner V1, DP > 1, other EP sizes, EPLB, and routed-experts capture. With EPLB or routed-experts capture on, the warmup forwards would pass dummy tokens to the load recording and the capture hook.

---

hits.title: [Kernel] Integrate DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE with fused shared experts
hits.body:
## Summary

Add a ModelOpt NVFP4 MegaMoE path backed by DeepGEMM, including fused BF16 shared-expert execution.

- Quantize NVFP4 activations and stage activation/scales/top-k directly into the symmetric buffer in one Triton launch.
- Transform routed NVFP4 weights/scales into the DeepGEMM layout.
- Fuse compatible BF16 shared experts; keep the ordinary shared path for unsupported modules.
- Keep symmetric-buffer allocation/rendezvous outside forward and CUDA Graph capture.
- Fail closed for unsupported router semantics, dtype, bias, LoRA, alignment, platform, DBO, or missing DeepGEMM APIs.
- Preserve the existing ModelOpt path unless `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` is selected.

Requires a DeepGEMM build containing the NVFP4 MegaMoE APIs from the merged [deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#409](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/409).

### Why this is not a duplicate

The related open Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4 changes target model-specific paths; this PR is the only open change integrating NVFP4 MegaMoE with the ModelOpt/RoutedExperts path used by GLM-5.2.

### Design and review fixes

- Replaced `scaled_fp4_quant` plus temporary tensors and four `copy_` calls with direct-to-symmetric-buffer NVFP4 staging.
- Folded FP4 quantization, E4M3 scale packing, top-k conversion, and padding masking into one launch.
- Cached the reciprocal activation global scale outside forward.
- Added fail-closed handling for `apply_router_weight_on_input` and other unsupported configurations.
- Restricted shared fusion to modules whose semantics are preserved; otherwise shared execution remains unfused.
- Fixed the real startup contract found on GB300: router IDs may be `int32` or `int64`, while the symmetric `topk_idx` output is `int64`.
- Expanded contract, padding, dtype, H=6144, and CUDA Graph replay tests.

## Test Plan

### Environment

- 8x GB300, two hosts x four GPUs, DP8/EP8 and TP1.
- Model: `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`.
- CUDA 13, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, FlashInfer `0.6.15.post1`.
- vLLM V2 model runner with compilation mode 0 (no `torch.compile`).
- FULL CUDA Graph requested; sparse MLA selects `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` at runtime.
- Maximum sequences per rank: 1024; maximum batched tokens: 16,384; prefix caching disabled.
- Performance revision: `8d37d14`; current PR head: `9febe8a2e`. Later commits add contract guards and tests, then remove redundant adapter state and over-strict weight-scale validation; they do not change the timed DP8/EP8, TP1 path.
- DeepGEMM revision: `0c067ed4` from the dependent PR.

### Serve recipe

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --max-num-seqs 1024 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL"}'
```

For the FlashInfer baseline, replace `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` with `--moe-backend auto --all2all-backend flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`.

### Workload and measurement

- [NVIDIA SPEED-Bench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/SPEED-Bench) `throughput_16k`, `low_entropy` category. Download it with:

  ```bash
  curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Skills/refs/heads/main/nemo_skills/dataset/speed-bench/prepare.py | \
    python3 - --config throughput_16k --output_dir ./speed-bench
  ```

- Deterministically sample exact 128-token windows across source rows without replacement. Each point uses `8 * M` distinct prompts.
- ISL `128`, OSL `256`, `temperature=0`, `ignore_eos=true`.
- M/rank: `1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024`; global request concurrency is `8 * M`.
- Send exactly M requests directly to each rank endpoint. Warm each point with one short request per rank, then run two formal repeats. The final DeepGEMM M1024 point uses three repeats.
- For each repeat, measure the common steady-decode interval from the latest first-token timestamp to the earliest request-completion timestamp. Count streamed output tokens in that interval and report aggregate throughput across all eight ranks. The table reports the median repeat.
- Model loading, JIT compilation, backend autotuning, CUDA Graph capture, prefill, first-token latency, and drain are outside the measured window.

## Test Results

### D-only: SPEED-Bench low entropy, 128 input / 256 output, DEP8

| M/rank | FlashInfer baseline (tok/s) | DeepGEMM fused (tok/s) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 532 | 560 | **+5.12%** |
| 2 | 982 | 1,030 | **+4.84%** |
| 4 | 1,778 | 1,860 | **+4.61%** |
| 8 | 3,227 | 3,404 | **+5.49%** |
| 16 | 6,182 | 6,533 | **+5.67%** |
| 32 | 11,787 | 12,422 | **+5.38%** |
| 64 | 22,040 | 23,606 | **+7.10%** |
| 128 | 41,878 | 44,571 | **+6.43%** |
| 256 | 68,145 | 76,152 | **+11.75%** |
| 512 | 96,883 | 108,828 | **+12.33%** |
| 1024 | 104,228 | 117,379 | **+12.62%** |


### P-only: random prompts, OSL=1, GB300 PCP8/EP8

| ISL | FlashInfer req/s | DeepGEMM req/s | Throughput gain | FlashInfer p50 TTFT | DeepGEMM p50 TTFT | p50 TTFT |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1K | 39.601 | 55.249 | **+39.51%** | 402.807 ms | 288.575 ms | **-28.36%** |
| 2K | 27.004 | 37.990 | **+40.68%** | 592.267 ms | 421.739 ms | **-28.79%** |
| 4K | 20.329 | 26.193 | **+28.84%** | 776.873 ms | 604.094 ms | **-22.24%** |
| 8K | 10.089 | 12.815 | **+27.01%** | 1539.304 ms | 1221.353 ms | **-20.66%** |

Every point completed all formal requests with zero failures. The initial sweep showed +38.12%/+41.91%/+29.93%/+28.72% throughput for 1K/2K/4K/8K; the repeat preserved the direction and magnitude at every point. Because `long_prefill_token_threshold=4096`, the 8K prompts were chunked; this flag was identical in both arms.

#### P-only serve recipe

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --enforce-eager \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --max-model-len 9216 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --long-prefill-token-threshold 4096 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

For the FlashInfer baseline, replace `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` with `--moe-backend auto`; all other serving flags are identical.

### Routing-imbalance sensitivity

The imbalance factor `x` is the busiest destination rank's received routed slots divided by the mean received slots across the eight destination ranks:

```text
x = max(slots_received_by_rank) / mean(slots_received_by_rank)
```

Thus, `1x` is perfectly balanced, while `2x`, `4x`, and `7x` mean that the busiest rank receives 2, 4, or 7 times the average routed slots. 
| Destination imbalance | DG gain at M32 | DG gain at M64 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1x | **+18.26%** | **+19.95%** |
| 2x | **+17.61%** | **+19.53%** |
| 4x | **+4.83%** | **+7.82%** |
| 7x | **-25.76%** | **-28.36%** |

## Accuracy

| Validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| B300 dense PyTorch-reference UT | **PASS** on all eight ranks; relative output differences `1.49e-6` to `2.16e-6` with finite outputs and per-expert alpha/A2 scale paths |
| B300 full-size fusion-order test | Fused versus unfused output was exactly identical; deliberately wrong `(routed + shared) * 2.5` ordering differed by `0.2979`, validating `routed * 2.5 + shared` |
| Targeted GB300 integration smoke | **PASS**: M=1 `int32` IDs, M=8 `int64` IDs, and semantic guards |
| Targeted vLLM GPU tests | **16/16 passed** |
| DeepGEMM boundary/adversarial | **42/42 passed**, M/rank 1-2048, max rel-L2 `0.005421` |
| DeepGEMM random fuzz | **22/22 passed**, M/rank 3-3073, max rel-L2 `0.002655` |
| DeepGEMM shared-only | **10/10 passed**, max rel-L2 `0.001134` |
| Real GLM-5.2 MoE layer replays | **75/75 passed**; fused was closer to FP32 in 69/75 layers |
| Deterministic E2E prompts | **16/16 exact** for each arm across two runs |
| 700-repeat long-context probe | All three arms produced the same token sequence and content |
| Initial paired GSM8K canary, fixed 100 questions, 5-shot | FI **93%**, DG fused **93%**; invalid responses **0%** in both arms |
| GSM8K, 100 questions, 5-shot | FI **95%**, DG unfused **94%**, DG fused **95%**; invalid responses **0%** |


<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR.
- [x] The test plan and commands.
- [x] The model-evaluation and performance results.
- [ ] (Optional) Documentation updates.
</details>




## Contribution notes

- AI assistance was used during implementation, debugging, review, benchmark analysis, and preparation of this PR description. The human submitter must review and understand every changed line and verify the final commands and results before merge.

## Overview

Day-0 support for Reflection's Beam-1.0 (`BeamForCausalLM`), a 501B-parameter MoE with 23B active parameters, and its DFlash2 drafter (`DFlash2BeamDraftModel`).

**This PR is now a tracking PR and is not meant to be merged.** It was split into the reviewable PRs below; everything on this branch is either in `main` or in an open slice.

## Status

| PR | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|
| #62042 | Router GEMM kernels for (5120, 256) and BF16 output in `ll_bf16_gemm` | ✅ Merged (2026-10-16) |
| #62052 | `beam` reasoning and tool parsers, `VLLM_BEAM_ALWAYS_CONSTRAIN_OUTPUT` | ✅ Merged (2026-10-16) |
| #62074 | Beam model and DFlash2 drafter (Blackwell kernels, standard TP all-reduce) | ✅ Merged (2026-10-19) |
| #62366 | Fused MNNVL all-reduce with Beam's sandwich norms and MoE finalize | 🔄 In review |
| #62073 | Attention DP + CuTeDSL NVFP4 MegaMoE (needs FlashInfer nightly); stacked on #62366 | 🔄 In review |

**What landed differs from this branch:**

- `BeamConfig` and the model follow the released `config.json` schema (`layer_types`, `mlp_layer_types`, per-type `rope_parameters`). Handling only pre-release checkpoints needed was removed, and switches the release never sets are fixed. Code built on this branch that reads the removed keys (for example `enable_sandwich_norm`, `mlp_only_layers`, `nope_layer_ids`, `moe_router_dtype`) must use the released behavior instead.
- The DFlash2 drafter no longer subclasses the Qwen3 DFlash classes.
- The DFlash `max_position_embeddings` override was dropped: the released drafter already matches the target.

**Remaining work:**

- Serving re-run on `main` (NVFP4 + DFlash2, TP8 GB200) with the released checkpoints. The numbers below were measured on this branch with the full stack, including the fused all-reduce.
- #62366: end-to-end before/after against `main`, and whether `allreduce.cu` (and #62073's `moe_finalize.cu`) stay runtime-JIT through FlashInfer or are built into vLLM.
- #62073: validation with FlashInfer nightly, which the MegaMoE paths and the DP-boundary test require.

## Validation (this branch, full stack)

**Serving:** Beam-1.0 NVFP4 + DFlash2 (7 draft tokens), TP8 on GB200, SPEED-Bench `throughput_1k` low-entropy subset, greedy decoding:

| Concurrency | Fixed draft (tok/s) | Adaptive (tok/s) | Acceptance length |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 708 | 707 | 3.71 → 3.61 |
| 128 | 15,012 | 16,632 | 3.68 → 3.23 |

**Prefill**, 4×GB300, 32K input / 1 output token:

| Configuration | Peak input throughput (tok/s) |
|---|---:|
| Attention DP + MegaMoE | 168.8K |
| TP4 | 98.7K |

**Decode/prefill kernels:** compared with the first implementation, TP8 batch-1 decode went from 8.95 ms to 3.30 ms per step (2.71×), and an 8 × 2K prefill from 328 ms to 176 ms (1.87×). Part of this comes from the fused all-reduce in #62366.

vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4 -tp 4 --max-num-seqs 128 \

hits.title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Prefer MegaMoE for supported local expert parallelism
hits.body:
## Purpose

For DeepSeek V4.1, resolve `--moe-backend auto` to `deep_gemm_mega_moe` for supported local expert-parallel deployments. Previously `auto` went through generic FusedMoE selection and never reached the model's MegaMoE path. In particular, TP4/DP1 with expert parallelism did not enable the model's sequence parallelism; the new selection enables it without requiring an explicit backend flag.

Resolve the choice during model configuration, before construction selects sequence-parallel and shared-expert paths. Preserve explicit backend choices. Restrict automatic selection to SM100-family CUDA devices with DeepGEMM enabled/available, MXFP4 experts, supported routing and dimensions, and a fully NVLink-connected local EP group. Leave other configurations on the existing selection path, including PP/CP, remote DP, Ray, speculative decoding and microbatching.

This changes backend selection only; it does not modify kernels or attention/indexer defaults. This should land after #57204 to avoid making the existing padding/duplicate-storage overhead the default. That padding change is not included in this diff.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open issues and PRs for DeepSeek/MegaMoE/default and auto-MoE selection, including PRs referencing #57204. No open PR implements this model-specific default selection. #40833 integrates generic MegaMoE support, #54049 integrates a FlashInfer MegaMoE implementation, and #57204 changes native MegaMoE padding; those are separate changes.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k deepseek_v41_auto_moe -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/config.py tests/test_config.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files vllm/model_executor/models/config.py tests/test_config.py --hook-stage manual
```

<details>
<summary>Real-checkpoint evaluation commands</summary>

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --revision dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277 \
  --served-model-name dsv41-gsm8k --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8003 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend auto \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching --language-model-only \
  --generation-config vllm --seed 123 \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"thinking":false}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'
```

After the server is ready:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m lm_eval run --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=dsv41-gsm8k,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8003/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,timeout=600,max_retries=2,max_gen_toks=1024,max_length=16384,seed=123 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=1024 temperature=0.0 do_sample=False "chat_template_kwargs={'thinking': False}" \
  --seed 123,123,123,123 --log_samples --output_path gsm8k-results
```

Repeat on parent commit `1085b64425` with `--moe-backend auto` for the original selection path. For this comparison, the parent model-configuration file was restored while all other runtime source files were identical. The PR configuration file was restored after evaluation.

</details>

## Test Result

25 configuration cases passed on GB200. Applicable pre-commit hooks and mypy 3.12 passed. Coverage includes eligible selection, explicit overrides, hardware/dependency/topology guards and unsupported model/parallel configurations.

Real checkpoint: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, four GB200 GPUs, TP4/DP1/EP4, `max_model_len=1048576`, FULL decode graphs, lm-eval 0.4.12. Full GSM8K, five-shot multi-turn chat, thinking disabled, greedy generation, 1024 output tokens, seed 123.

| Selection | Correct / 1319 (flexible extraction) | Accuracy | Strict-match accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Parent `auto` → FlashInfer TRT-LLM MXFP4/MXFP8 | 1272 | 96.4367% | 79.8332% |
| Proposed `auto` → DeepGEMM MegaMoE | 1269 | 96.2092% | 78.3927% |

All 1319 document, prompt and target hashes match. Eight baseline errors became correct and eleven baseline-correct answers became errors: a net difference of three questions in this single paired run. This does not establish statistical equivalence across workloads.

Both runs retain upstream attention/indexer defaults: the server selected `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41` with the NVFP4 attention cache format and the FP8 indexer. No separate attention, indexer or padding patches were included. The 1M model limit does not mean GSM8K tested 1M-token prompts. Startup and graph capture succeeded for both arms.

Validated source commit `cac37db059`, parent `1085b64425`, with precompiled CUDA/runtime assets from that exact parent commit. The initial checkout reused older runtime assets and failed before serving; the results above come from the matched runtime after those setup failures were resolved.

Memory tradeoff: these TP4/EP4 runs reported 81.46 GiB/GPU allocated during model loading for MegaMoE versus 71.03 GiB/GPU for the former default. This is the model-loading allocation reported by vLLM, not total serving peak memory; automatic MegaMoE selection can leave less room for KV cache. Source accounting attributes about 7.03 GiB/GPU to routed FP4 weight padding (2304 → 2560), 1.32 GiB/GPU to retained original shared weights alongside padded fused copies, and 0.99 GiB/GPU to shared-weight replication versus TP4 sharding, before scale/layout differences. #57204 removes the first two causes; the full 10.43 GiB gap should not be interpreted as intrinsic MegaMoE overhead. These component estimates are calculated from checkpoint dimensions, not a runtime tensor census.

## AI assistance

Codex assisted with implementation, validation, and this description. Woosuk Kwon requested the default change after reviewing the TEP backend-selection and sequence-parallel behavior.

hits.title: [ROCm][DSv4] EPLB for the AITER MegaMoE backend
hits.body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4's AITER MegaMoE backend (`--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe`) rejected `--enable-eplb`. This PR hooks it into vLLM's EPLB, the same way the DeepGEMM MegaMoE path does. On DeepSeek-V4-Pro, ATOM's EPLB for the same kernels cuts the long-context prefill step by 14.6%. The last three commits are generic EPLB changes that MegaMoE EPLB needs on ROCm; each can be split out.

## Claims

- `--enable-eplb` works with `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe`. It rebalances by permutation only (`num_redundant_experts=0`), as ATOM does.
- `EPLBConfig.max_rebalances` (new; default 0 = no limit, unchanged behaviour): stop after N rebalance points and keep the placement.
- ROCm: `torch_nccl` expert-weight transfers no longer hang RCCL.
- ROCm: the "skip rearrange" check no longer vetoes every MegaMoE rebalance.

Usage (sync EPLB; `torch_nccl` requires `use_async: false`):

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend aiter_mega_moe --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput \
  --enable-eplb --eplb-config '{"use_async": false, "communicator": "torch_nccl", "max_rebalances": 2}'
```

## Validation

The numbers below come from a lab branch: vLLM 77154ca6 plus this change, alongside unrelated local patches. Setup: DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 8x MI355X, TP1 x DP8 attention, EP8 AITER MegaMoE, DSpark draft. EPLB ran with window 100 / interval 200 and at most 2 rebalances. The lab counted only engine steps that contain a prefill; that counting is not part of this PR, and a larger window and interval in engine steps give a similar cadence.

Prefill probe: each of the 8 ranks prefills 8,107 new tokens at ~108K context next to 16 decoding requests:

| | EPLB off | EPLB on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| prefill step (ms, median of 6 rounds) | 1102 | 944 (-14.3%) |
| MegaMoE combine wait per step (ms, mean over ranks; worst rank) | 167 (180) | 36 (55) |
| MegaMoE stage1 / stage2 per step (ms) | 165 / 231 | 164 / 225 |
| decode step at 16 req/rank (ms) | 55.6 | 55.5 - 56.3 |

ATOM gets -14.6% on the same probe. The gain is the combine wait: the expert GEMM time per rank stays the same, but the busiest rank no longer holds every rank back.

- gsm8k (lm-eval, real speculative decoding) with EPLB on: 0.9719 / 0.9727 (two runs).
- A rebalance moves ~2.5k of each rank's 2.9k expert slots across 61 layers. The first one took 5.2-5.7 s in the probe and load runs, ~2.3 s of it RCCL connection setup, and up to ~12 s under heavier live traffic. Later ones take ~2.5 s. ATOM's migration takes 5.4 s.
- Stress test under load: 34 forced full-permutation rebalances while serving 32 concurrent requests, 0 request errors, correct greedy answers before and after.
- Unit tests (CPU): `tests/distributed/test_eplb_utils.py` (ring pairing, cap, per-layer imbalance) and `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_mega_moe.py -m cpu_test` (weight views, remap before the runtime choice, MixtureOfExperts registration; importing it needs a ROCm build).

E2e and validation on this upstream branch are still to be added.

## Details

**MegaMoE EPLB (commit 1).**
- The AMD `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` implements `MixtureOfExperts` over the MegaMoE layers only; other AMD MoE paths keep `num_moe_layers == 0`.
- `DeepseekV4AiterMegaMoEExperts.get_expert_weights()` returns per-expert row views of the finalized w13 / w2 weights and scales. The a16w4 shuffles are within-expert, so EPLB rewrites rows in place. MegaMoEV2 reads the weights by pointer at every launch, so CUDA graphs stay valid.
- `forward()` maps logical to physical ids with `eplb_map_to_physical_and_record` (load recording included) before the runtime choice. The fixed-slot decode runtime (#61262) and the prefill runtime therefore both dispatch physical ids. Per-expert slot capacity does not depend on placement.
- Redundant experts are rejected.
- The DSpark draft is not registered: its MoE only sees decode-sized batches, and it keeps its own static placement.

**`max_rebalances` (commit 2).** Every rebalance point blocks all EP ranks. A skipped point still pays an all-reduce, a host sync and the policy, and an applied one moves weights for seconds. When the placement only needs to adapt once (ATOM uses `ATOM_EPLB_MAX_REBALANCES=2` here), the cap stops further points; the remap stays and load recording stops.

**ROCm ring P2P order (commit 3), root cause.**
- `rearrange_expert_weights_inplace` posts a layer's sends and receives as one `batch_isend_irecv`: about 340 ops per rank here.
- With RCCL 2.27.7 on MI355X this deadlocks on some transfer plans. The trigger is a rank that sends to many peers while it also exchanges with one peer in both directions.
- It is deterministic for a given plan. A torch-only 8-GPU reproducer hangs on the same seeded plans every time, with one batch per layer and also with ATOM-style 32-expert chunks. In serving it killed the engine at the execute timeout during the first rebalance.
- The fix: on ROCm, `TorchDistNcclEplbCommunicator` runs the layer as ring batches. Batch d holds the sends to rank + d and the receives from rank - d, in the same d order on every rank, so a send and its receive meet in the same batch with one peer per direction.
- Results: 4k seeded plans in the reproducer and 4k plans through `rearrange_expert_weights_inplace` (random and default-policy plans), no hang, 0 misplaced rows, ~47 ms per layer.
- A no-op `EplbCommunicator.prepare_transfer()` hook lets the communicator create its group's communicator with a collective first, because a ring batch need not involve every rank. Other platforms keep one batch per layer.

**Per-layer skip check (commit 4).** The ROCm-only check skips a placement unless the rank-load imbalance improves by 5%. It summed each rank's load over all layers before taking max/mean, so per-layer skews on different ranks cancelled out. MegaMoE's per-layer max/mean of ~1.77 (to ~1.12 after rebalancing) read as 1.063 -> 1.118, and every rebalance was skipped. Each MoE layer waits for its busiest rank, so the check now uses the sum over layers of max over the sum over layers of mean, the same quantity `log_balancedness` reports.

**Not included / follow-ups.**
- This PR keeps the profile-time dummy rearrangement. With `torch_nccl` it all-gathers one layer of expert weights, and its load all-reduce creates the EP group's RCCL communicator, which MoRI otherwise never uses. Together that costs ~12 GiB of KV cache per rank here: 95.7 -> 83.3 GiB with EPLB on, vs 93.8 GiB in the lab with that step skipped. This can follow separately.
- `pynccl` transfers are not ring-ordered.
- No redundant experts.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and this description; the measurements come from the author's runs.

hits.title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Optimize MegaMoE staging and NVFP4 cache gathers
hits.body:
## Purpose

Reduce DeepSeek V4.1 MegaMoE/MegaAttention prefill overhead: tile multiple tokens
per MegaMoE staging program for sufficiently large inputs, and size the NVFP4
gather grid by request count and output capacity. Keep conservative launch
choices for small inputs. Both transformations preserve the existing arithmetic
and add no persistent buffers.

Dispatch uses eight-token staging tiles from 64 tokens, otherwise one token.
On GB200 at H5120, forced eight-token tiles regress 2–16-token kernels, tie at
32, and improve from 64 onward (both scale layouts):

| Tokens | Native staging us | Eight-token tile us |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | 2.400 | 2.752 |
| 32 | 2.880 | 2.816 |
| 64 | 3.328 | 3.136 |
| 128 | 4.672 | 3.296 |
| 8192 | 175.616 | 32.416 |
| 16384 | 348.993 | 60.736 |

NVFP4 gathers retain 128 workers for short rows and chunks of >=16 requests.
Otherwise use `min(2048 // num_reqs, max(128, compressed_capacity))` workers.
At 100K gathered rows, 1/2/4/8-request kernel latency falls by 88%/76%/50%/18%;
16/32 requests are unchanged. The caller passes a view of the compressed region
so SWA workspace does not inflate its capacity. No allocation, device-to-host
synchronization or actual-KV decode dispatch is added.

Kernel sweeps use CUPTI, CUDA graphs and cold L2, checking bitwise equality
before timing. Final branch boundary/stride checks are recorded below.

## Performance and validation

GB200×4, DEP4/MegaMoE/MegaAttention, model revision
`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1.
Earlier paired ten-sample fixed-forward confirmations with matching tuned GEMMs:

| Workload per DP rank | Baseline ms | Candidate ms | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Q16K, KV100K | 415.559 | 400.955 | 3.51% |
| B31Q1 + B1Q8K, KV100K | 224.438 | 207.711 | 7.45% |

Mixed baseline SD 9.124 ms versus candidate 0.697 ms; all samples retained.
The earlier three-sample mixed screen improved 6.14%. B8Q2K improves 1.73%;
decode/draft are essentially unchanged. No new model or workspace buffers.
These are synthetic fixed-forward GPU timings, not serving throughput.

Matched full real-weight GSM8K: 1272→1271 /1319 (96.44→96.36% flexible extraction;
7 improve, 8 regress). DSpark acceptance length 3.8281→3.8289. Real-prefill
traces confirm both changed paths execute. Both accuracy arms carry the separate
sparse-remap correctness guard, which is not included in this PR.

GPU validation at `e2a2356a6229`: **29 staging tests and 24 gather tests pass**.
The gather cases cover 1/8/32 requests, 70/128/129/2051 rows, partial gathers,
non-contiguous request strides, untouched bounds, and CUDA-graph replay after
changing lengths in persistent buffers.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py \
  -k 'fused_input_staging or stages_shared_scale_tma_layout' -q -rs
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
  -k v41_nvfp4_gather_matches_insert -q -rs
```

All pre-commit hooks pass. The follow-up removes only benchmark scripts;
production code and correctness tests retain the validated contents. Final dispatched-kernel checks preserve short gathers
and small staging inputs. At H5120/N64, the final staging comparison is
3.360→3.264 us; the gain near the boundary is modest. At H7168/N64,
3.712→3.168 us supports the same cutoff. Large-input gains remain intact.
The earlier real-weight quality evaluation is reused: this dispatch refinement
preserves the evaluated arithmetic; the narrower view changes launch bounds only.

Validation commit `e2a2356a6229` full-model checks pass with finite outputs and zero
eager/graph, changed-input and restored-input replay errors:

- Q16K: 400.490 ms (three samples), consistent with the earlier confirmation.
- DEP B32 adaptive verification, draft length 5 and seeded lengths 1–6:
  112 total tokens; same-instance original/automatic staging measures
  **18.310→18.285 ms (0.14%)**, with matched inputs, KV and GEMM tactics.
  A post-timing trace confirms all 40 staging calls: summed kernel time
  144.00→112.16 us; MegaMoE time remains 11.703 ms in both arms.

An earlier unpaired B32 check measured 30.287 ms with high spread. It is retained
as an unexplained slow run, not used to estimate the staging effect. The paired
check above isolates staging and does not reproduce that regression. Compilation
is excluded from timing and guarded against during timed work.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR found for tiled DeepSeek MegaMoE staging or CUDA NVFP4 gather sizing.
#56720 sizes a ROCm FP8 gather grid and explicitly preserves CUDA dispatch;
this change targets the separate CUDA NVFP4 branch. #43592 targets MiniMax-M2
prepared-input fusion rather than this DeepSeek staging kernel. #55109 fixes
block-table strides; #57489 adds gfx950 FP4 attention. Neither implements these
CUDA launch heuristics.

AI assistance was used to implement, benchmark and test this change.

hits.title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Pad shared experts for native MegaMoE fusion
hits.body:
## Purpose

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56217

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's 2304-wide shared expert cannot fuse with MegaMoE's routed experts padded to 2560. Pad shared weights with zeros and unit scales to enable fusion in all 40 layers, preserving checkpoint-shaped parameters and the unsupported-layout fallback.

Extends #53040. Checks of #45861 and related open PRs found no fix for this padding gap; #53567 and #54049 cover different paths.

AI assistance was used for implementation, testing, and documentation.

## Test Plan

### Deploy

Use a fresh server per arm: `VLLM_DISABLE_DSV4_MEGAMOE_SHARED_EXPERT_FUSION=1` for serial shared experts, `0` for fused. The omitted load-time hook verifies fusion state on all 8 ranks.

```bash
export MODEL=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=bond0 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=bond0 NCCL_DEBUG=WARN
export VLLM_DISABLE_DSV4_MEGAMOE_SHARED_EXPERT_FUSION=0
uv run --active --no-project python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve "$MODEL" \
  --served-model-name dsv41-bench --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8032 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --seed 2026 --generation-config vllm \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256],"max_cudagraph_capture_size":256}'
```

### Benchmark

Workloads follow #53040, plus 8192/1024 at C16. V4.1 uses block size 128 and FP8 indexer cache.

```bash
# Use a separate result directory for each arm.
export RESULT_DIR=results/dsv41-fused
mkdir -p "$RESULT_DIR"
bench() {
  uv run --active --no-project python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \
    --backend vllm --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8032 --endpoint /v1/completions \
    --model dsv41-bench --tokenizer "$MODEL" --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
    --trust-remote-code --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len "$1" --random-output-len "$2" \
    --max-concurrency "$3" --num-prompts "$4" \
    --random-range-ratio 0 --random-prefix-len 0 --request-rate inf \
    --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 42 --num-warmups 2 \
    --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,95,99 \
    --save-result --save-detailed --disable-tqdm \
    --result-dir "$RESULT_DIR" --result-filename "$5.json"
}
for repeat in 1 2 3; do bench 128 256 1 8 "decode-128-256-c1-r$repeat"; done
for repeat in 1 2 3; do bench 1024 128 1 8 "decode-1024-128-c1-r$repeat"; done
for repeat in 1 2 3; do bench 1024 128 64 128 "balanced-1024-128-c64-r$repeat"; done
for repeat in 1 2 3; do bench 8192 32 16 32 "prefill-8192-32-c16-r$repeat"; done
bench 8192 1024 16 100 kimi-8192-1024-c16-r1
```

<details>
<summary>GSM8K evaluation reproduction</summary>

Use lm-eval 0.4.12, the same fusion flag, and a fresh server per arm.

```bash
export MODEL=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=bond0 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=bond0
export NCCL_DEBUG=WARN
export VLLM_DISABLE_DSV4_MEGAMOE_SHARED_EXPERT_FUSION=0
uv run --active --no-project python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve "$MODEL" \
  --served-model-name dsv41-gsm8k --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8031 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --generation-config vllm --seed 123 \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"thinking": false}'
```

Run the full test split in the lm-eval environment, with separate output directories:

```bash
OPENAI_API_KEY=EMPTY uv run --active --no-project python -m lm_eval run \
  --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=dsv41-gsm8k,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8031/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,timeout=600,max_retries=2,max_gen_toks=1024,max_length=16384,seed=123 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=1024 temperature=0.0 do_sample=False "chat_template_kwargs={'thinking': False}" \
  --seed 123,123,123,123 --log_samples --output_path results/gsm8k-fused
```

</details>

## Test Result

31 tests passed on B200. Ruff, typos, mypy 3.10/3.12, and applicable pre-commit checks passed; nonmatching Actionlint and requirements-compilation hooks were skipped.

All 8 ranks confirmed 0 → 40 fused layers. Model-load memory increased from 41.47 to 43.34 GiB/rank (+1.87 GiB) because the original shared parameters remain allocated.

8×B200, TP8/EP/SP, FP8 KV, 16K context. `vllm bench serve`: 2 warmups/run, median of 3 runs except 8192/1024 (1 run), no profiler. All 1,256 requests succeeded with the requested token counts. Both arms used source `30aa0ade39ab6625674865f578fae19a49cf3e43` + this patch, native build `e7edf17cea217e52701f913cd8491fcacf2d9490`, and PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130.

| Input / output | Concurrency | Requests × runs | Output tok/s: serial → fused | Change | Mean TPOT ms: serial → fused | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128 / 256 | 1 | 8 × 3 | 122.6 → 134.3 | +9.6% | 8.115 → 7.402 | -8.8% |
| 1024 / 128 | 1 | 8 × 3 | 109.2 → 121.0 | +10.9% | 8.178 → 7.455 | -8.8% |
| 1024 / 128 | 64 | 128 × 3 | 2853.9 → 3359.2 | +17.7% | 16.851 → 14.567 | -13.6% |
| 8192 / 32 | 16 | 32 × 3 | 192.7 → 226.1 | +17.3% | 48.804 → 41.806 | -14.3% |
| 8192 / 1024 | 16 | 100 × 1 | 1292.1 → 1428.8 | +10.6% | 10.449 → 9.449 | -9.6% |

| Input / output, concurrency | Mean TTFT ms: serial → fused | Change | Median ITL ms: serial → fused | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128 / 256, C1 | 18.57 → 17.80 | -4.1% | 8.107 → 7.392 | -8.8% |
| 1024 / 128, C1 | 133.85 → 110.82 | -17.2% | 8.162 → 7.439 | -8.9% |
| 1024 / 128, C64 | 706.90 → 558.69 | -21.0% | 11.038 → 10.285 | -6.8% |
| 8192 / 32, C16 | 1109.92 → 937.88 | -15.5% | 9.170 → 8.387 | -8.5% |
| 8192 / 1024, C16 | 912.06 → 815.41 | -10.6% | 9.082 → 8.357 | -8.0% |

Negative latency changes mean lower latency. C1 has only 8 requests/run, so tail-latency estimates are limited.

C64's first run hit quantization JIT in both arms. Excluding it from both changes the throughput gain from +17.7% to +16.6%.

| GSM8K metric | Serial shared | Fused shared | Change (percentage points) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| flexible-extract | 96.21% (1269/1319) | 96.13% (1268/1319) | -0.076 |
| strict-match | 78.17% (1031/1319) | 79.23% (1045/1319) | +1.061 |

hits.title: [Perf][EPLB][DSv4] Add a symm_mem weight-migration backend and fuse MegaMoE replica mapping
hits.body:
## Overview

This PR makes EPLB cheaper for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, running DP attention with EP MegaMoE on multi-node NVLink. It does three things:

- adds an opt-in `symm_mem` weight-migration backend;
- fuses EPLB's logical→physical replica mapping and expert-load recording into the DeepGEMM MegaMoE staging kernels;
- takes async EPLB's host work off the decode critical path.

Not a duplicate. No open or merged PR adds a symmetric-memory EPLB backend or fuses the MegaMoE mapping. #61176 and #61839 enable EPLB for the ROCm AITER MegaMoE backend. Related: #61767 (`cpu_all_reduce_`, reused here), #57549, #56716, #61643.

## Claims

- EPLB raises decode throughput on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB200 NVL72 by +3.7% at DEP32 with 72 req/rank and +7.7% at DEP32 with 128 req/rank. At DEP16 the step is about 3% shorter, but the throughput gain is within run-to-run noise.
- `symm_mem`: senders push expert rows into the receiver's `expert_buffer`, which is allocated in CUDA symmetric memory. There is no staging buffer, and it needs no memory beyond `expert_buffer`. Cross-node peer copies run at about 800 GB/s, against about 88 GB/s for NIXL, and a 40-layer rearrangement transfers in 0.3–0.6 s at DEP32.
- MegaMoE layers no longer launch a separate EPLB mapping kernel, which saves 5–6 µs per layer. The replica choice is shared with the router through one Triton helper, so physical ids and load counts match `eplb_map_to_physical_and_record` exactly.
- Async EPLB no longer adds a GPU→host sync to the decode loop. It also raises on every rank when the worker fails on any rank, instead of stalling.

## Validation

Hardware: GB200 NVL72, 4 GPUs per node.

Serving setup: DSpark with 5 draft tokens, MRV2, FULL CUDA graphs, async scheduling.

EPLB setup: `{"num_redundant_experts": <DP>, "window_size": 1000, "step_interval": 3000, "use_async": true, "communicator": "symm_mem"}`, i.e. one redundant expert per rank.

Workload: decode only, coding-agent prompts with mean ISL ≈ 85k (prefix-cached), 16k output tokens with `ignore_eos`, and requests pinned evenly to DP ranks. Throughput is the output rate over the window in which every request is decoding.

Off and on arms ran interleaved (ABAB) on the same nodes. These runs used a branch of nightly fe4df3df (2026-10-12) with this change set and #61767, before the rebase and without the second commit.

| Config | EPLB off (tok/s) | EPLB on (tok/s) | Δ | Welch t |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DEP16, 72 req/rank | 223.6k ± 2.0k (n=4) | 228.1k ± 4.2k (n=4) | +2.0% | 2.0 (not resolved) |
| DEP32, 72 req/rank | 419.5k ± 1.3k (n=4) | 435.1k ± 5.8k (n=4) | +3.7% | 5.3 |
| DEP32, 128 req/rank | 500.7k ± 5.1k (n=3) | 539.4k ± 9.7k (n=3) | +7.7% | 6.1 |

- DEP16 step time, p50 of 2000-step windows at full batch, same build: 24.34 / 24.28 ms off vs 23.61 / 23.25 ms on.
- At DEP32 with 128 req/rank, one pass per arm is excluded. A host stall unrelated to EPLB cut that pass by 13–34%.

Per-step breakdown, DEP32 with 128 req/rank:

| | EPLB off | EPLB on |
|---|---|---|
| Step time (CUDA events, unprofiled) | 38.8 ms | 36.5 ms |
| GPU idle at the step boundary | 0.27 ms | 0.27 ms |
| Main-model MegaMoE (5 s CUDA profile) | 18.1 ms | 13.4 ms |
| All other kernels (same profile) | 21.5 ms | 21.2 ms |

The GPU never waits on the host, so the MegaMoE saving turns into step time. MegaMoE is about 40% of the step, which caps the end-to-end gain.

Microbenchmarks (GB200):

- **Fused EPLB staging**, one MoE layer, hidden 5120, top-k 6, 384 logical experts. Each arm is timed as a CUDA graph replay, median of 200. Outputs, ids and load counts match main bit for bit in every case.

  | Format | Tokens | Physical experts | main: `torch.where` + map kernel + staging | Fused | Saved |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | MXFP8 | 432 | 400 | 9.4 µs | 4.2 µs | 5.1 µs |
  | MXFP8 | 768 | 416 | 11.0 µs | 4.7 µs | 6.3 µs |
  | NVFP4 | 432 | 400 | 49.5 µs | 44.0 µs | 5.5 µs |
  | NVFP4 | 768 | 416 | 49.1 µs | 43.8 µs | 5.3 µs |

  That is about 0.2 ms per decode step across 40 MoE layers.
- **Weight-migration bandwidth**, 2 nodes, one MegaMoE layer of 25 experts (470 MB):

  | Path | Bandwidth |
  |---|---|
  | `symm_mem` peer copies, intra- or cross-node over multi-node NVLink | ~808 GB/s (bulk), ~294 GB/s (100 per-tensor copies) |
  | NIXL, cross-node | ~88 GB/s (UCX picks RoCE, not multi-node NVLink) |
  | NIXL, cross-node, `UCX_TLS=cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,tcp` | ~0.12 GB/s (TCP) |

- **MegaMoE kernel time under serving load**, DEP16 with 72 req/rank, layers 2–40: p50 per call drops 12.6–14.0% across three profiled runs (222→194 µs). Layer 1 is excluded because it absorbs cross-rank arrival skew.

Tests on this branch, one GB200 node with 4 GPUs. They ran before the rebase onto 64175d3827; the 5 newer commits on main touch none of these files.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py` (incl. `test_prepare_megamoe_eplb_matches_router_under_graph_replay`) | 110 passed |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py -k eplb` | 18 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py` | 35 passed, 14 skipped (NIXL not installed, XPU) |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py -k nixl`, NIXL installed | 7 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_utils.py`, `test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py` | 6 passed, 28 passed |
| `tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py`, `test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py` | 13 passed, 7 passed |

GSM8K on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (one node):
- Setup: 5-shot, 1319 questions, temperature 0, `num_redundant_experts=16`, `window_size=100`, `step_interval=300`. Every arm rearranged all 40 layers four times during the eval.
- Command: `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 5 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64`

| Arm | Accuracy (2 passes) | 40-layer rearrangement |
|---|---|---|
| EPLB off | 0.898, 0.901 | — |
| `symm_mem` | 0.897, 0.895 | 2.9–3.3 s |
| `symm_mem`, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | 0.889, 0.883 | 2.9–3.3 s, no sync error |
| `nixl` | 0.892, 0.886 | 2.7–3.2 s |

The EPLB-off and `nixl` arms ran on the commit before the final cleanup, which does not touch either path. Within one node, `symm_mem` and NIXL (CUDA IPC) move weights at a similar rate; `symm_mem`'s advantage is across nodes over multi-node NVLink.

## Details

**`symm_mem` backend**
- The receive buffer is one symmetric `uint8` buffer per EP group, set up with a single rendezvous and carved into per-tensor views. The backend checks the NVLink/MNNVL domain before allocating.
- Senders and receivers derive each receive row from the global placement with the same helper, so `add_recv` is a no-op. Push backends get every rank's rows through a new `recv_rows` argument to `set_transfer_context`. This argument is optional and other backends ignore it.
- Each `execute()` runs two CPU barriers. GPU spin barriers can deadlock against MegaMoE's cooperative launches.
- Rejected with elastic EP. The buffer lives outside the caching allocator, so sleep mode does not free it.

**Fused mapping**: `fused_moe/eplb_triton.py` holds the replica hash, map lookup and gated load count. The MXFP8/BF16 and NVFP4 staging kernels call it, and so does the router kernel. Routed-experts capture still sees logical ids.

**Async EPLB**
- Per-layer maps are committed with pinned non-blocking copies, and the worker thread fences `expert_buffer` reuse.
- Balancedness stats are read back non-blocking and logged in order once they land.
- `should_record_tensor` is rewritten only when its value flips.
- The per-step "all ranks ready" check runs over `cpu_all_reduce_`. A gloo ring all-reduce costs several ms per step at DP16/DP32.

**Also**
- `logical_to_physical_map` is sized to R+1 slots unless elastic EP is on.
- `compute_logical_maps` is vectorized.
- DeepSeek V4.1 decoder-replay padding and dummy rows are marked as padding, which complements #61643.

**CI**: the `symm_mem` execution tests need NVLink peers. They are added to the optional 8×H100 "Distributed DP + EP" job; the 4×L4 EPLB job skips them. The MegaMoE parity test needs SM100.

**Limitations**
- In mixed prefill/decode serving, per-rank prefill imbalance bounds the step. There, EPLB mostly lowers tail TTFT rather than raising throughput.
- Likely rebase overlap with #61786, #59168 and #41141. Offline placements without elastic EP (#41141) could exceed R+1 replicas.
