hits.title: [Kernel][Perf] Add H100 tuned configs for Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B to the batch-invariant matmul table
hits.body:
## Overview

In short: in batch-invariant (BI) mode (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`), every bf16 linear layer and the lm_head run the Triton kernel `matmul_kernel_persistent` instead of cuBLAS. Its tile comes from a per-GPU table, and the Hopper table only has the five Qwen3-1.7B shapes (measured on an H20), so Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B run the default 128x128x64 tile on H100. This PR adds H100-measured entries for their 8 TP=1 shapes to the `"hopper"` family.

With BI on, on an H100 SXM:
- `vllm bench latency` is 1.85-2.79x faster than main.
- The BI tax (latency with BI on / latency with BI off) drops from 2.13-2.99x on main to 1.03-1.20x with this PR.
- GSM8K stays within 0.5 standard error (SE) of main.

Related: tracker [#27433](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/27433), same kind of table as [#53247](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53247), [#57456](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57456), [#58495](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58495).

## Key results

- 8 new `(N, K)` entries in `_BATCH_INVARIANT_MATMUL_TUNED_CONFIGS["hopper"]`: gate_up/down/lm_head of Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B plus their shared qkv/o. Existing entries and other families are not touched.
- One `BLOCK_K` per shape, so a row's K-reduction order does not depend on M. Checked bit for bit through the real `matmul_persistent` dispatch: 2028/2028 cases identical.
- Kernel (H100 SXM, cold L2): geomean 2.03x vs main over 80 (shape, M) cases, 2.89x at M <= 64; the slowest case is 1.00x (Qwen3 gate_up at M=2048, 827 vs 828 us). At M <= 64 the kernel is now 0.90-1.12x of cuBLAS time (main: 1.48-4.09x).
- E2E latency with the flag on (fresh process per run, 2 interleaved rounds):

| model, workload | BI=0 (s) | BI=1 main (s) | BI=1 this PR (s) | PR vs main | BI tax main -> PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B, 32 in / 128 out, bs 8 | 0.854 | 2.452 | 0.881 | 2.78x | 2.87x -> 1.03x |
| Llama-3.1-8B, 1024 in / 32 out, bs 8 | 0.403 | 0.859 | 0.444 | 1.94x | 2.13x -> 1.10x |
| Qwen3-8B, 32 in / 128 out, bs 8 | 0.893 | 2.668 | 0.956 | 2.79x | 2.99x -> 1.07x |
| Qwen3-8B, 1024 in / 32 out, bs 8 | 0.414 | 0.917 | 0.495 | 1.85x | 2.22x -> 1.20x |

- `vllm bench serve` (1024 in / 128 out, 1000 prompts, rate inf, 3 interleaved rounds, req/s; rounds 1 / 2 / 3, then the mean). Llama-3.1-8B gains 13.6%. Qwen3-8B does not change; Details explains why (the execution mode these shapes switch on, not the tiles).

| model | BI=0 | BI=1 main | BI=1 this PR | PR vs main | throughput tax main -> PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B | 28.29 / 28.35 / 28.32, 28.32 | 21.62 / 21.69 / 21.61, 21.64 | 24.71 / 24.57 / 24.48, 24.59 | +13.6% | 1.31x -> 1.15x |
| Qwen3-8B | 27.43 / 27.47 / 27.54, 27.48 | 21.45 / 21.48 / 21.51, 21.48 | 21.50 / 21.48 / 21.47, 21.48 | 0.0% | 1.28x -> 1.28x |

- GSM8K (5-shot, BI=1): every difference to main is within 0.5 SE.

| model | main strict / flexible | this PR strict / flexible |
|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B | 0.7180 ± 0.0124 / 0.7832 ± 0.0114 | 0.7119 ± 0.0125 / 0.7839 ± 0.0113 |
| Qwen3-8B | 0.8764 ± 0.0091 / 0.8779 ± 0.0090 | 0.8741 ± 0.0091 / 0.8757 ± 0.0091 |

The raw output for every row of these tables is under Validation.

## Validation

**Setup.**
- GPU: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 SXM, 132 SMs, power limit 700 W of 700 W.
- Software: driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130, triton 3.8.0.
- main = 307c5844ad. PR = main + this commit, applied on the box with `git am` (same diff).
- main and PR are the same checkout, switched with `git checkout`. Every run is a fresh process.
- Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct checkpoint: `unsloth/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`, an ungated copy. It has the same architecture and layer shapes as `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`; its config.json adds `pad_token_id`. I did not compare the weights against the gated repo.
- [#61118](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61118) merged after this base. It enables Inductor's `batch_invariant` flag. It can only change the torch.compile arms (main, and PR + torch.compile under Details). It does not change this PR's default breakable-graph mode, because that mode does not run Inductor.

**Bitwise.**
- Path: `matmul_persistent` on the PR tree, all 13 hopper shapes.
- Check: a probe row at rows 0, M/2 and M-1 must equal the same row computed at M=1.
- M values (39): 1-17, every bucket edge ±1, 100, 1000, 3000 and 4096.
- 2 seeds. Weight as `w.t()` (the linear layout) and as a contiguous `(K, N)` tensor.
- Result: 2028/2028 identical, 0 mismatched.

**Tests** (PR tree):

```
pytest -v tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py                                  # 35 passed, 2 skipped
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-8B pytest -v tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py            # 22 passed
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=unsloth/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct pytest -v tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py  # 22 passed
```

**Kernel**, `matmul_persistent` main -> PR, us per call.
- Each point is a CUDA graph of 4-24 launches. The script aims for about 2 ms of work per replay (4 to 20 launches), rounded up to whole cycles of the weight copies.
- The launches cycle over enough weight copies to read >= 4x L2 per pass.
- main is the mean of two runs, one before and one after the PR run. The two runs agree within 0.98-1.08x.

All 10 buckets per shape, with both main runs and the PR config, are in `kernel/report_mean_main_vs_pr.md` in the attached logs.

**Latency** (`vllm bench latency`):
- 2 rounds per arm. Every run is a fresh process. Arms are interleaved per round.
- Arms: BI off = `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0` on main; main and this PR = `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on that tree.

```bash

```

The raw output of all 24 runs is in the four "Raw output: vllm bench latency" dropdowns at the end of this section.

**Serve** (`vllm bench serve`):
- 3 rounds per arm, with a fresh server for every run. Arms are interleaved per round.
- Each server first gets a 64-prompt warmup run, which is not measured.


## Details

**These shapes also change the execution mode.**
- Since [#57586](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57586), BI mode checks the model's qkv/o/gate_up/down shapes against the device's table.
- If one shape is in the table (bf16, unquantized, CUDA, not `enforce_eager`, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` unset), the model runs with breakable CUDA graphs and without torch.compile.
- In that mode the tile is looked up from the runtime M. Under torch.compile the lookup is frozen to one tile at trace time ([#54243](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54243)).
- So this PR moves Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B to breakable graphs, in addition to the new tiles.

To separate the two effects, I ran two extra arms, 1 round each (raw output in the "mode diagnostic" dropdown under Validation):
- main + breakable graphs (`VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`): the mode change only.
- PR + torch.compile (`VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`): the new tiles. qkv/o/gate_up/down are frozen to one tile; lm_head runs outside the compiled forward and keeps the per-M lookup.

| model | arm | latency 32/128 (s) | latency 1024/32 (s) | serve (req/s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B | main | 2.452 | 0.859 | 21.64 |
| Llama-3.1-8B | main + breakable graphs | 2.423 | 0.856 | 21.34 |
| Llama-3.1-8B | PR + torch.compile | 1.824 | 0.667 | 24.81 |
| Llama-3.1-8B | PR (default: breakable graphs) | 0.881 | 0.444 | 24.59 |
| Qwen3-8B | main | 2.668 | 0.917 | 21.48 |
| Qwen3-8B | main + breakable graphs | 2.639 | 0.926 | 20.30 |
| Qwen3-8B | PR + torch.compile | 2.120 | 0.763 | 22.66 |
| Qwen3-8B | PR (default: breakable graphs) | 0.956 | 0.495 | 21.48 |

What the table shows:
- The gain comes from the tiles. Breakable graphs alone change latency by about 1%.
- Per-M tile selection makes decode fast: 0.881 s, against 1.824 s with one frozen tile.
- In all four latency workloads, breakable graphs win by 1.5-2.2x.
- In the prefill-heavy serve workload, torch.compile wins:
  - Dropping Inductor costs 5.5% on Qwen3-8B and 1.4% on Llama-3.1-8B.
  - With breakable graphs, the new tiles only win back that 5.5% on Qwen3-8B.
  - PR + torch.compile is ahead by 5.5% (Qwen3-8B) and 0.9% (Llama-3.1-8B), 1 round each.
- This trade-off comes from the [#57586](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57586) gate, not from these entries. I did not change the gate.
- With this table, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` gives Qwen3-8B serving +5.5% over main.

**How the entries were picked.**
- Search space and BLOCK_K rule are the same as [#57456](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57456):
  - BLOCK_K {32, 64, 128} x BLOCK_M {16, 32, 64, 128} x BLOCK_N {32, 64, 128, 256} x warps {4, 8} x stages {2, 3, 4, 5}.
  - Timed at M in {1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 256, 512, 1024, 2048}.
  - One BLOCK_K per shape, by the decode-weighted score. Then the fastest tile per bucket with that BLOCK_K.
- Two differences from [#57456](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57456):
  - Cold-L2 timing. Each point is a CUDA graph that cycles over enough copies of `(x, w)` to read >= 4x L2 per pass. o (32 MB) and qkv (48 MB) fit in the 50 MB L2, so warm timing would make them look faster than in the model.
  - The bitwise gate runs on all 10 buckets, not 4. A probe row at rows 0, M/2 and M-1 must equal the M=1 output.
- Before the gate, the top 3 configs per (bucket, BLOCK_K) were re-timed over 5 interleaved passes.
- Margins:
  - 43 of 80 picks beat the runner-up by more than the pass-to-pass spread.
  - The other 37 are within the spread. 20 of them are within 1%. The rest are at M >= 256, where the spread is larger.
  - Every pick is faster than main's default tile. In 77 of 80 buckets the margin is larger than the spread; the other 3 are 1.04-1.07x.
- Result: BLOCK_K = 64 for Llama gate_up, 128 for the other 7 shapes.

**Not a duplicate.**
- [#60034](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60034) (draft) tunes five other Hopper shapes (17408x5120, 5120x8704, 8192x5120, 5120x3072, 124160x5120) for M <= 16. No overlap.
- [#54503](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54503) and [#55752](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55752) change how the M bucket is selected at runtime. They work with any table entries.
- [#59952](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59952) (split-K for N <= 64) replaces the table lookup in `matmul_persistent` with a fixed heuristic. If it lands as written today, these entries and the existing Ada/Hopper/Blackwell/SM120 entries no longer set the tile. The [#57586](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57586) gate still reads the table, so they would still switch the execution mode.
- [#53446](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53446) (closed) proposed H100 NVL configs for the Qwen3-1.7B shapes already in the table. This PR adds new shapes only. It does not change existing entries.

**Limitations.**
- Measured on H100 SXM only. The `"hopper"` key also covers H100 PCIe/NVL, H200, H800 and H20. For these shapes they run the default tile today. I have not measured them.
- With these entries, the jit monitor logged at most one `matmul_kernel_persistent` compile per process. In latency and serve runs it came during warmup, never in a measured iteration (none in the Llama decode latency runs). In lm_eval, which has no warmup, it came on the first request; that changes timing only, not scores. main logged none.
- TP > 1 per-rank shapes are not included.
- The table and the [#57586](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57586) gate use only `(N, K)`. Other bf16 models with the same shapes also get these tiles and the mode change. Example: Mistral-7B-v0.3 has exactly the layer shapes of Llama-3.1-8B. I have not measured those models.
- CI: the H100 Batch Invariance job runs `test_batch_invariance.py` (Qwen3-1.7B, plus needle tests on DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8) and the RMSNorm and LoRA-shrink tests. It does not run `test_matmul_batch_invariant.py`, and none of its models use these shapes. So only the validation above covers these entries.

I used Claude Code for this change. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and benchmarks above myself.

hits.title: [Hardware][NVIDIA] Add GB10 fused-MoE fp8 tuning config (E=128, N=704 — Gemma 4 26B A4B)
hits.body:
## Purpose

Add the first fused-MoE Triton tuning config for **NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark)** for the `E=128, N=704, fp8_w8a8` (per-tensor, no block_shape) MoE layer shape — the shape of **Gemma 4 26B A4B FP8-dynamic** (e.g. `RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-dynamic`, compressed-tensors). Without a device-specific config, GB10 falls back to heuristic defaults and logs `Using default MoE config. Performance might be sub-optimal!` at every engine start.

Not a duplicate: the only GB10 configs on main today are from #52502 — `E=256,N=512` and `E=512,N=512` with `block_shape=[128,128]` (DeepSeek-family shapes). `E=128,N=704` currently exists only for B200 / H100 / RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell — GB10 owners running Gemma 4 26B get heuristics.

## Config

- Tuned on a single DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), TP=1, with `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --model ... --tp-size 1 --dtype fp8_w8a8 --tune`, vLLM `0.27.2rc1.dev113`, Triton `3.7.1`, torch `2.13.0+cu130`.
- Keys `3 / 12 / 24` cover decode for this deployment: serving uses MTP-style speculative decoding with `num_speculative_tokens=2`, so each decode step processes `3 × num_seqs` tokens (max `MAX_NUM_SEQS=8` → M=24; runtime lookup picks the nearest key).
- Keys `256 / 1024 / 4096` cover chunked-prefill token counts.

## Tuning caveat (transparency)

To fit the tuning window (each Triton compile is slow on this ARM box: full 1920-config sweep ≈ 70 min **per batch size**), the search space was pruned per batch size before running `--tune`: for `num_tokens ≤ 64` only `BLOCK_SIZE_M ≤ 32`, `GROUP_SIZE_M ≤ 32`, `num_stages ≤ 4`; for `num_tokens ≥ 256` only `BLOCK_SIZE_M ∈ [32,128]`, `BLOCK_SIZE_N ≥ 64`, `BLOCK_SIZE_K ≤ 128`, `num_stages ≥ 3`. Rationale: `BLOCK_SIZE_M ≥ 128` with ≤24 decode tokens is pure padding (grid is per-expert blocks), and deep pipelines only pay off in the compute-bound regime. A full-space sweep may find marginally better entries.

## Test Plan

- [x] Config is picked up at engine start: log line `Using configuration from .../E=128,N=704,device_name=NVIDIA_GB10,dtype=fp8_w8a8.json for MoE layer`; the `Using default MoE config` warning is gone.
- [x] Serving verified stable end-to-end on the tuning box (OpenAI chat + tool calls + reasoning parser, ~20h of mixed traffic including a long background pipeline workload).

## Test Result

End-to-end A/B on the same box (identical engine config, quiet machine, streaming bench, deterministic prompt, repeats=3):

| Metric | Heuristic default | This config | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 decode tok/s | 36.4 | **62.2** | **+71%** |
| c=1 TTFT (median) | 192 ms | **128 ms** | **−33%** |
| c=2 aggregate tok/s | 72.2 | **125.4** | **+74%** |
| c=4 aggregate tok/s | 182.6 | 168.3 | −8% (within thermal noise) |

Real-traffic check (Prometheus, matched-concurrency windows ≈1.2 running seqs, long-context background pipeline with 10–30k-token prompts): inter-token latency p50 66.5→64.4 ms (−3%), p90 97.7→87.6 ms (−10%), per-request throughput ≈ +11% — at long context the attention share of a decode step is large, so the MoE-kernel win is diluted; the large gains above are for short-context requests where MoE dominates the step.

## Note for maintainers (tuning-script finding)

While tuning on Triton 3.7, `clear_triton_cache()` in `benchmark_moe.py` is a **silent no-op**: it probes `triton.runtime.cache`, which does not exist in 3.7 (real in-process JIT cache lives on `JITFunction.device_caches`). The worker therefore accumulates every compiled variant (~5 MB × ~2000 ≈ 10 GB RSS) and Ray's memory monitor kills it mid-run. If others report tuning runs dying on GB10/ARM, this is likely why.

hits.title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Enable the fused all-reduce + mHC boundary at TP2
hits.body:
## Motivation

The fused CuTe DSL Lamport all-reduce + mHC post/collapse/RMSNorm (#57643, #58586) only runs at TP4. The Blackwell single-node recipes now default to TP2 (vllm-project/recipes#1002), so at TP2 every small-batch sublayer boundary still runs a separate all-reduce plus unfused mHC. The kernel is already parametrized by the TP world size, so this PR admits TP2 in `supports_mhc_all_reduce` (TP8 stays off) and extends the tests to TP2.

## Evaluation

Setup: 2 × GB200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

**Correctness**
- GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions): main 0.901, this PR 0.901.

**Performance**: `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, ISL 1024 / OSL 512, no speculative decoding, mean of 3 seeds.

| Concurrency | TPOT p50 (ms) main → PR | Output tok/s main → PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.19 → 4.48 (−13.8%) | 184.6 → 213.0 (+15.4%) |
| 2 | 5.58 → 4.93 (−11.7%) | 347.7 → 390.7 (+12.4%) |
| 4 | 6.10 → 5.25 (−13.9%) | 607.2 → 701.5 (+15.5%) |
| 8 | 6.86 → 6.08 (−11.3%) | 1092.2 → 1212.9 (+11.1%) |
| 16 | 8.48 → 7.64 (−9.9%) | 1767.1 → 1919.2 (+8.6%) |
| 32 | 10.59 → 10.55 (−0.4%) | 2786.3 → 2658.8 (−4.6%, one outlier run) |
| 64 | 13.44 → 13.72 (+2.1%) | 4364.5 → 4346.2 (−0.4%) |

Swapping the two arms' GPUs (and NUMA nodes) gives the same picture: TPOT changes by −12.1%, −13.9%, −10.8% and +0.7% at C1, C4, C16 and C64. TTFT is unchanged.

With DSpark (recipe default, k=5):

| Concurrency | ITL p50 (ms) main → PR | Output tok/s main → PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7.12 → 6.49 (−8.8%) | 616.7 → 680.6 (+10.4%) |
| 2 | 8.37 → 7.27 (−13.2%) | 986.9 → 1149.0 (+16.4%) |
| 4 | 9.63 → 8.33 (−13.6%) | 1423.3 → 1497.0 (+5.2%) |

At C≥8, DSpark steps exceed the 16-token fused limit, so the fused path is not taken.

## Notes

- TP2 + DSpark on main can hit the autotune `Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic` startup crash, which is unrelated to this PR. #58165 fixes it.

hits.title: [DCP] Add FlashInfer fused A2A backend for decode context parallelism
hits.body:
## Summary

Adds FlashInfer's fused MNNVL all-to-all (LL128) kernel as an alternative backend for the DCP **a2a-reduce** exchange, on top of the merged packed-NCCL a2a path (`--dcp-comm-backend a2a`, #41160). The kernel replaces the two `dist.all_to_all_single` exchanges of the packed path with a single fused `decode_cp_a2a_alltoall`.

The backend defaults to **automatic selection by hardware** (`--dcp-a2a-backend auto`), with an opt-in override:

- **Blackwell (sm_100+)** → FlashInfer fused LL128 A2A (captured under CUDA graph, where it beats the NCCL pack → `all_to_all` → unpack chain).
- **Everything else** → NCCL packed (unchanged behavior). In eager / non-Blackwell, FlashInfer's per-call overhead makes it ~3–5% slower, so it is not used there.
- **`--dcp-a2a-backend {auto,nccl,flashinfer}`** (default `auto`) lets users force the kernel. `nccl`/`flashinfer` override the auto choice; forced `flashinfer` still falls back to NCCL if the MNNVL workspace can't initialize (never crashes). Ignored unless `--dcp-comm-backend a2a`.

The FlashInfer MNNVL workspace is allocated lazily the first time an attention backend selects the A2A combine path (before CUDA-graph capture); if that fails (no NVL fabric / IMEX, e.g. non-NVL72 cross-node) it logs a warning and **falls back to NCCL packed** — no user action, no crash.

**Files (7 changed):**
- `vllm/distributed/dcp_alltoall_flashinfer.py` (new): MNNVL workspace manager (alloc + init + CPU barrier; `enable_pdl=False` to match TRT-LLM), cached per CP group.
- `vllm/v1/attention/ops/dcp_alltoall.py`: dispatcher routes `dcp_a2a_lse_reduce` to FlashInfer or NCCL; 16-byte-align pad; reuses the existing pack/unpack + Triton LSE-combine. Hosts `ensure_dcp_a2a_backend()` — honors `--dcp-a2a-backend`; `auto` consults compute capability + cudagraph mode; workspace pre-init + graceful NCCL fallback.
- `vllm/config/parallel.py`, `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py`: the `--dcp-a2a-backend` option (`DCPA2ABackend` literal, `ParallelConfig` field, CLI plumbing, ignore-warning when set without `a2a`).
- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/{flash_attn,flashinfer}.py` and `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py`: call `ensure_dcp_a2a_backend()` lazily when the A2A DCP-combine path is selected (the MLA layer is where MLA models — the DCP targets — select it).

## Why this is not a duplicate

Open PRs searched (`decode context parallel a2a`, `flashinfer alltoall`, `dcp comm backend`): #45964 (MLA query replication for decode) and #47915 (TokenSpeed MLA DCP decode) change *what* is computed for MLA decode, not *which comm kernel* performs the a2a-reduce; #47355 (draft) overlaps DCP indexer streams. None add a FlashInfer fused A2A kernel as a DCP a2a-reduce backend. This builds on the merged `--dcp-comm-backend a2a` and adds a faster kernel for it on Blackwell.

## Design note for reviewers — auto by default, override available

The default (`--dcp-a2a-backend auto`) picks the kernel by hardware: FlashInfer only where it is CUDA-graph-captured on Blackwell with an MNNVL fabric, NCCL packed otherwise. Because that choice is fully determined, `auto` is the recommended path. The `nccl`/`flashinfer` values are provided for users who want to pin the kernel (benchmarking, forcing NCCL on Blackwell, etc.); a forced setting that can't run (e.g. `flashinfer` where the MNNVL workspace can't init) still falls back to NCCL rather than crashing.

## When each backend is used

| Situation | Backend |
|---|---|
| Blackwell (sm_100+), **full-cudagraph decode**, MNNVL workspace OK | FlashInfer LL128 A2A |
| Non-Blackwell (Hopper, …) | NCCL packed |
| Eager, or piecewise-only cudagraph (decode not full-graph captured) | NCCL packed |
| Blackwell without MNNVL fabric (non-NVL72 cross-node) | NCCL packed (graceful fallback) |

The selection is gated on `cudagraph_mode.decode_mode() == FULL` (the a2a-reduce is a decode-time op), so eager and piecewise-only decode fall to NCCL where FlashInfer's per-call overhead would otherwise regress. This table describes `--dcp-a2a-backend auto`; `nccl` forces the NCCL column and `flashinfer` forces the FlashInfer kernel (still falling back to NCCL if the MNNVL workspace can't init).

## Tests

Served DeepSeek-R1 671B with `--dcp-comm-backend a2a`:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --dcp-comm-backend a2a --attention-config.backend FLASHINFER_MLA \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL"}' --trust-remote-code
```

- **Functional**: on Blackwell (B200/B300/GB200) the auto-select engages FlashInfer (MNNVL workspace `mnnvl=True` on all ranks; fused kernel confirmed active during decode) and serves; on Hopper it uses NCCL packed unchanged; the graceful NCCL fallback is exercised when the MNNVL workspace cannot initialize (e.g. non-NVL72 cross-node).
- **Accuracy** — this change only alters how the a2a-reduce is *transported* (the all-to-all moves the same data; the existing Triton LSE-combine does the same math), so the reduced values are numerically equivalent to the NCCL packed path modulo floating-point reduction order — there is no expected accuracy effect. gsm8k 5-shot exact-match was equal between FlashInfer A2A and NCCL packed within sampling noise on both DeepSeek-V2-Lite and DeepSeek-R1 (FLASHINFER_MLA + cudagraph FULL).
- **Performance** — DeepSeek-R1 671B (FP8, MLA), FLASHINFER_MLA + cudagraph FULL, DCP=8, ISL=512/OSL=256, measured with `vllm bench serve` (warmup per point). Mean-TPOT improvement (time per output token — the decode-step latency this a2a-reduce change acts on), FlashInfer A2A vs NCCL packed, across a concurrency sweep:

| Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Single-node (8×B300) | +3.0% | +1.9% | +2.4% | **+5.0%** | +3.5% | +1.0% | +0.6% |
| Cross-node (GB200-NVL72, 2 nodes) | +1.5% | +1.7% | +1.8% | **+2.7%** | +1.9% | −0.6% | +1.0% |

(Absolute TPOT ranges ~9.6 ms at c=1 to ~26 ms at c=64.) The improvement **peaks at moderate concurrency (c=8: +5.0% single-node, +2.7% cross-node) and tapers toward parity at high concurrency** — consistent with the fused LL128 kernel helping most in the latency-bound regime (small per-step a2a messages) and mattering less once the exchange becomes bandwidth-bound. TTFT is a prefill metric, unaffected by this decode-time change (parity). In eager mode (no cudagraph) FlashInfer is ~3–5% slower (per-call dispatcher overhead) — which is why auto-select restricts it to Blackwell + cudagraph; cross-node additionally requires the NVL72 IMEX fabric (falls back to NCCL otherwise).

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance (Claude). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above. Commits carry `Signed-off-by` (DCO) and `Co-authored-by: Claude`.

hits.title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Restore the fused query RMSNorm + MXFP8 quantization path
hits.body:
## Purpose

`can_fuse_query_quant` decides whether the DeepSeek-V4.1 attention block may hand `wq_b` a pre-quantized query, letting `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm_quant` do the q/kv RMSNorm and the MXFP8 quantization in one kernel. It probed `linear.input_quant_key`. #53793 renamed that attribute to the private `_input_quant_key` and introduced `get_input_quant_key` as its reader, but this call site was not updated, and it is the last one in the tree still reading the old name. The gate has been unconditionally `False` since that rename, so every layer runs a BF16 `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm` followed by a standalone `MXFP8QuantizeSwizzled` over the query — exactly the pair the fused kernel exists to replace.

Read the capability through `get_input_quant_key`, and pass `launch_pdl` to the fused kernel's launch. The kernel already compiles in `gdc_wait()` / `gdc_launch_dependents()` from its `LAUNCH_PDL` constexpr, but without the launch attribute Triton issues an ordinary launch, so the kernel cannot start before its predecessor retires and the wait is inert. Its siblings `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm`, `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` and the Qwen4 PLE/HC kernels pass both. The fused path is CUDA-only by construction, since `can_fuse_query_quant` returns `False` off CUDA, so the new kwarg is never reached on ROCm.

This restores a lost fusion; it does not change model output. The fused kernel reproduces the separate-kernel FP8 bytes, swizzled scales and normalized KV bit for bit.

## Duplicate-work check

No issue tracks this, so issue-number checks are not applicable. Open-PR searches covered `can_fuse_query_quant`, `input_quant_key`, `get_input_quant_key`, `query_quant deepseek_v41`, `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm`, `launch_pdl triton` and `deepseek_v41 pdl`. Nothing else touches `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/ops/query_quant.py`. #53793 performed the rename that stranded this gate. #55505 extends the same contract with input scales and does not change how the key is read. #48086 also adds a missing `launch_pdl`, but in `deepseek_v4/common/ops/fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py`, for a `TypeError` on non-PDL hardware rather than a lost overlap. #54063 and #53151 teach ROCm AITER kernels to consume `QuantizedActivation` instead of fixing a producer gate.

## Test Plan

```bash
PATH=/usr/local/cuda-13.1/bin:$PATH .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/core/test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/ops/query_quant.py
```

The existing suite already encodes this gate: `test_shared_query_quant_preserves_projection` asserts `can_fuse_query_quant` is true for the two FlashInfer MXFP8 kernels and that the pre-quantized `wq_b` projection matches the BF16 path at `rtol=0, atol=0`. It needs Blackwell plus a FlashInfer that can JIT, so `nvcc` must be on `PATH` or the whole group skips, which is how the regression went unnoticed.

Two standalone harnesses, not included in the diff, produced the numbers below. One times the isolated production chain `fused_wqa_wkv` GEMM → q/kv RMSNorm (+ query quantization) → `wq_b` GEMM and compares outputs bitwise before timing. The other serves the model and sweeps client concurrency, running both code versions inside one job so they share a node, with the order counterbalanced across two jobs.

## Test Result

Standalone commit `20538d465a`, based on `9d75dd4544`. **73 tests passed** in 107 s on GB200. On `main` the same file reports **24 failed**, all of them `test_shared_query_quant_preserves_projection` cases failing at `assert can_fuse_query_quant([linear, linear])`, so no new test was needed. Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including ruff, ruff format, typos and mypy 3.10.

Model output is unchanged. The microbenchmark checked FP8 data, swizzled scales, normalized KV and the downstream `wq_b` GEMM output for bitwise equality against the two-kernel path at all 14 shapes before timing, and the projection test asserts the same at `rtol=0, atol=0`. No accuracy evaluation is claimed, because the change cannot move a logit.

### Performance
Serving: `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` with `indexer_kv_dtype=mxfp4` and `indexer_sparse_logits`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-num-seqs 128`, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. Client is `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, 1024 input and 256 output tokens, `--ignore-eos` and `--temperature 0` so every request runs exactly 255 decode steps. Concurrency 1 is repeated 10 times and the others 5 times; each cell is the median of per-run medians. The two columns of raw ITL are the two jobs.

| Concurrency | Base ITL (ms) | Patched ITL (ms) | ITL Gain |
|------------:|--------------:|-----------------:|---------:|
| 1   | 5.020 / 5.055   | 4.983 / 5.037   | 0.55% |
| 8   | 6.321 / 6.357   | 6.255 / 6.295   | 1.01% |
| 32  | 8.313 / 8.325   | 8.309 / 8.142   | 1.12% |
| 256 | 12.153 / 12.157 | 12.076 / 12.127 | 0.44% |

All eight paired measurements favour the patched build and swapping the order flips no sign. Concurrency 8 is the most trustworthy row: the two jobs agree at 1.05% and 0.97%, and 48 tokens per step is the shape where the microbenchmark predicts 69.7 us out of a 6.32 ms step, or 1.10%. 


## AI assistance

Claude Code assisted with the investigation, the benchmarks and this description. Juntian Liu requested this PR after reviewing the root cause, the measured gains and the benchmark caveats.

hits.title: [Bug]: DeepGemm accuracy auto-disable (_DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL_EXCLUDED_MODEL_TYPES) does not apply to the FP8 MoE path
hits.body:
### Your current environment

- Hardware: NVIDIA GB10, **SM121 / compute capability 12.1** (also relevant to SM120 generally)
- vLLM **0.26.0** (standard PyPI wheel, aarch64), torch 2.11.0+cu130, `--enforce-eager`, TP=1
- Model: `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` — `model_type: **qwen3_5_moe_text**`, 256-expert FP8 MoE

### 🐛 Describe the bug

vLLM correctly identifies that DeepGemm is inaccurate for this model type and logs so at startup:

```
WARNING [vllm.py:1008] Auto-disabled DeepGemm for model_type=qwen3_5_moe_text on Blackwell.
  DeepGemm E8M0 scale format causes accuracy degradation for this architecture.
  Falling back to CUTLASS. To disable DeepGemm globally, set VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0.
```

…and then **selects DeepGemm anyway for the MoE layers**:

```
INFO [fp8.py:405] Using DEEPGEMM Fp8 MoE backend out of potential backends:
  ['AITER', 'FLASHINFER_TRTLLM', 'FLASHINFER_CUTLASS', 'DEEPGEMM', 'TRITON', 'MARLIN', ...]
```

The auto-disable sets `quant_config.use_deep_gemm = False` (`vllm/config/vllm.py`), and
`qwen3_5_moe_text` **is** present in `_DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL_EXCLUDED_MODEL_TYPES`
(`vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`) — so the denylist is doing its job. But `use_deep_gemm` appears to have
**no references anywhere under `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/`**; the FP8 MoE backend
selector honors only the `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM` / `VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM` env vars. Net effect: the
denylist covers dense linear layers only, and the MoE layers — where the accuracy concern for an MoE
model actually matters most — still run DeepGemm.

So the warning is truthful about dense layers and silently wrong about MoE.

### Why this surfaced now

**PR #43477** ("Enable DeepSeek V4 and GLM-5.1 on SM120", shipped v0.24.0) added
`is_device_capability_family(120)` to `deep_gemm.py`. Prior to that, the SM100-family gate meant
DeepGemm was never *eligible* on SM121, so this gap was latent. The FP8 MoE backend priority list
itself is unchanged — DeepGemm simply became eligible and started winning.

Consistent with this, the original accuracy fix **#37804** reasoned that "MoE layers are unaffected
(already use FLASHINFER_TRTLLM)" — which holds on SM100 but **not** on SM121, where
FLASHINFER_TRTLLM is gated out (#43906).

### Impact

1. **Accuracy** — the exact degradation #37804 set out to prevent still applies to this model's MoE
   layers on SM120/121.
2. **Performance** — measurable on our hardware. Forcing Triton MoE (matching what vLLM 0.20.1
   selected) recovered most of a regression vs 0.20.1: median TPOT went 37.3 → 34.9ms at
   concurrency 1 and 43.7 → 39.3ms at concurrency 4 for this model.

### Expected behavior

The `_DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL_EXCLUDED_MODEL_TYPES` denylist should gate the FP8 **MoE** backend
selection as well as dense linear layers — i.e. `Fp8MoeBackend` selection should consult the same
`use_deep_gemm`/model-type exclusion rather than only the env vars.

### Workaround

`--moe-backend triton` (or `VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`). We shipped `--moe-backend triton`.

### Related

- **#47169** (open) is the *same gap in the warmup path* ("DeepGemm warmup ignores auto-disable"),
  reported on SM120 with a GB10/SM121 reproducer in the comments — likely the same fix area.
- **#37804** (closed) — origin of the denylist.
- **#43477** — made DeepGemm SM120-family eligible.
- **#41306** (open) — maintainer-confirmed MoE backend-selection perf regression of a similar shape.

### Note on SM121 specifically

On SM121 the alternatives to Triton for FP8 MoE all appear unusable, which is why `--moe-backend
triton` is the only workaround we found: FLASHINFER_TRTLLM gated to SM100 (#43906), VLLM_CUTLASS has
no SM120/121 CollectiveBuilder (#43507), MARLIN produces corrupt output on GB10 (#49546), HUMMING
crashes at startup (#49554).

hits.title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Small-head sparse decode on SM90
hits.body: ## Purpose On SM90, FlashMLA's sparse decode tiles query heads by 64 (the WGMMA M dimension). A DeepSeek V4.1 TP8 rank owns only 8 heads (16 at TP4), so it pads them to 64 and spends most of the tensor-core work on padding. This adds a Triton sparse decode kernel that tiles heads by 16 with `tl.dot` (mma.sync), reads the existing packed FP8 MLA cache directly, and recovers parallelism by splitting the key set across programs, merging the partial results with log-sum-exp. **Why it is faster at small batches.** At a few decode tokens per step, FlashMLA launches roughly one CTA per token and each CTA does 64-head work for 8 real heads. This kernel launches `tokens × splits` programs, each doing 16-head work over its share of keys. The best split count depends on both token count and key width: 32 splits at ≤3 tokens fills the GPU, but by 8 tokens 8 splits wins because the merge cost and per-program gather overhead dominate. `_pick_config` encodes this measured table. At larger batches the step becomes gather/dequant-bound rather than MMA-bound, so removing the padding no longer helps and FlashMLA is kept. **Dispatch** (automatic, no flag): SM90, 8 or 16 local heads, decode only, and | Layer key width (SWA + compressed top-k) | Uses this kernel at | Otherwise | | --- | --- | --- | | ≤256 (SWA-only layers) | ≤16 decode tokens per step | FlashMLA | | >256 (compressed layers, `index_topk=512`) | ≤12 decode tokens per step | FlashMLA | The gate is decode tokens per rank per step (≈ batch × (1 + spec tokens)), so the gain is limited to **low-concurrency decode**. It does not depend on context length, since sparse attention reads a fixed number of keys per token. Prefill always uses FlashMLA. **JIT warmup:** both launches register every split config, `HAS_EXTRA` variant and DSpark SWA width with the startup JIT warmup, so no Triton compile happens on the serving path. Related to #48168. **Not a duplicate:** I checked the issue discussion and open PRs for #48168 and for small-head sparse decode; none implements this SM90 decode path. #57673 has since been reworked into an opt-in backend that reuses this PR's decoder (with attribution) but does not add the automatic FlashMLA dispatch. #55866 targets FA4 sparse MQA on *Blackwell*, #51403 targets *ROCm*. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py -k small_head -q python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_small_head_decode.py --heads 8 16 --topk 0 64 512 --rounds 3 pre-commit run --all-files ``` End-to-end on 8× H20 (one node), TP8, DSpark K=2, same flags as our production deployment except `--max-model-len 32768`. Both arms ran on the same node and the same image, back-to-back: ```bash vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --seed 42 \ --max-concurrency {1,2,4,8,16,32} lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \ --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn --gen_kwargs temperature=0 ``` ## Test Result ### End-to-end (8× H20, TP8) Median ITL is per decode step; concurrency 1–4 falls inside the gate (≤12 tokens/step with K=2). | Concurrency | Stock median ITL | This PR | Δ ITL | Stock tok/s | This PR tok/s | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 8.99 ms | 8.37 ms | **−6.8%** | 239.6 | 264.4 | | 2 | 10.96 ms | 9.87 ms | **−9.9%** | 365.5 | 400.8 | | 4 | 13.91 ms | 13.11 ms | **−5.7%** | 574.2 | 621.9 | | 8 | 19.52 ms | 19.39 ms | −0.7% | 825.7 | 824.7 | | 16 | 27.48 ms | 27.13 ms | −1.3% | 1135.1 | 1178.9 | | 32 | 41.05 ms | 41.29 ms | +0.6% | 1510.6 | 1522.3 | Throughput also reflects DSpark acceptance length, which varied by run (2.06–2.23 stock vs 2.14–2.31 this PR), so ITL is the cleaner signal. **GSM8K** (full 1319, 5-shot chat, greedy, flexible extract): stock **89.99%** (1187), this PR **89.92%** (1186), stderr ±0.83%. Per question, 19 flip to correct and 20 flip to wrong, consistent with split-K reduction order changing near-tie greedy tokens. ### Operator benchmark (1× H20) 108 configurations (tokens 1–16/24/32 × heads 8/16 × top-k 0/64/512), CUDA graphs, cold-L2 input rotation, median of 3 alternating rounds, CUDA-event timing. Every configuration inside the gate is faster than FlashMLA; none regresses. | Key width | Gate | Speedup inside gate | Outside gate | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | SWA + top-k 0 / 64 | ≤16 tokens | 1.31–2.14x | FlashMLA (kernel would be 1.09–1.40x at 24, ~1.0x at 32) | | SWA + top-k 512 | ≤12 tokens | 1.06–1.42x | FlashMLA (kernel would be 0.90–0.94x at 16–32) | **JIT warmup (8× H20, TP8, DSpark K=2):** with `--jit-monitor-mode warn`, 92 requests at concurrency 1–8 all succeeded with zero small-head kernel compiles after startup; warmup compiles 8 decode + 3 merge variants in 2.3 s on one GPU. **Correctness:** 44 focused tests pass on H20 (FP32 reference and FlashMLA comparisons, 64/128-token pages, 8/16 heads, non-contiguous views, invalid/empty rows, CUDA graph replay, dispatch at the gate boundary). Pre-commit passes. > All GPU results use the vLLM 0.30.0 image with this PR's kernel and dispatch patched in, not an exact-head install. CI results are pending. - [x] Human submitter reviews every changed line and independently runs the tests. - [ ] Full focused suite on an exact-head install, and CI. - [x] Repeat the end-to-end A/B with interleaved runs to tighten the ITL numbers. --- AI assistance: OpenAI Codex and Claude were used to implement, tune, benchmark, and validate this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

hits.title: [Attention] Portable Triton sparse-MLA fallback for SM12x (consumer Blackwell)
hits.body:
## Purpose

DSA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.2) currently have **no working sparse-attention backend on
consumer Blackwell** (SM12x: RTX 5090, GB10): the native FlashMLA sparse kernels
(`vllm._flashmla_C`) only build for sm90/sm100, and the sole SM12x option,
`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`, livelocks under sustained load — GPUs pin at 100 % with zero
output until the NCCL watchdog kills the server. Fixes #51921 (on SM12x).

This makes the `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` backend work on SM12x by binding portable **Triton**
implementations of `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` / `flash_mla_with_kvcache` when the native extension
can't serve the device. The kernels are from #49026 (@marksunner, validated there on
sm_121/GB10) — this PR is that work rebased onto current main as a first-class code path
instead of that PR's runtime monkeypatch, with its model-side diffs dropped (main already has
that content). Supersedes/continues #49026 — happy to hand back or co-drive.

## Scope

This path covers **DeepSeek-geometry sparse MLA** — `qk_rope_head_dim = 64`, i.e. the
512 NoPE + 64 RoPE = **576** head layout: DeepSeek-V3.2/V4.1 and GLM-5.2. The Triton kernels
and the `fp8_ds_mla` 656-byte per-token entry are built around that 576 layout
(`get_supported_head_sizes() == [576]`).

**Not covered:** NoPE MLA models (`qk_rope_head_dim = 0`, `head_size = 512`) such as
GLM-5.3-Flash. Those are correctly rejected at the head-size gate and need the `pe_dim != 64`
work in #55277 / #53969 *in addition to* this PR. Thanks to @haqishen for confirming this
boundary on real SM120 hardware (see comments).

Changes:
- `ops/flashmla.py`: `_use_triton_sparse_mla()` (auto on SM12x; `VLLM_TRITON_MLA_SPARSE`
  forces on/off) selects the Triton binding; `is_flashmla_sparse_supported()` reports True
  there; `get_mla_metadata` returns `(None, None)` (the Triton kernels self-schedule).
- New files: `sm12x_sparse_mla_attn.py`, `sparse_mla_kernels.py`, `sparse_mla_env.py`,
  `ops/deepseek_v4_ops/*` — kernels + helpers from #49026, unchanged.
- `flashmla_sparse.py`: capability 12 allowed on the Triton path; %16 fp8-decode head padding
  there (64-head models at TP=8 have 8 heads/rank — 64-padding wastes 87 % of attention
  compute); b12x fused fast path with clean fallback.
- `sparse_attn_indexer.py`: DeepGEMM not hard-required on the Triton path (fallbacks exist).
- `envs.py`: `VLLM_TRITON_MLA_SPARSE*` registered.
- **Recommended runtime knob:** set `VLLM_SPARSE_MLA_SPLITK=32` on SM12x — it enables the
  split-K decode path and is a large single-stream decode win (see Test Result). The backend
  now logs a one-time hint when it is left unset.

**All changes are no-ops on sm90/sm100** unless `VLLM_TRITON_MLA_SPARSE=1` is set explicitly.

## Test Plan

End-to-end serving on 24× RTX 5090 (3 hosts, TP=8 × PP=3), GLM-5.2-NVFP4,
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, driven by `vllm bench serve`
(1K-in/256-out latency cell @ c1, then a c16 throughput cell; repeated full passes incl.
10K-token prompts). This load reproduces the #51921 livelock on stock v0.26.0/v0.28.0 within
minutes, so it discriminates cleanly between the two paths.

## Test Result

| | stock (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`) | this PR's path (`FLASHMLA_SPARSE` + Triton) |
|---|---|---|
| latency cell (c1, n=8) | first request spins **660 s** (GPUs 100 %, zero output), engine dead before the next cell | **8/8** — TTFT 5.3 s, **TPOT 41 ms** |
| throughput cell (c16) | never reached | **64/64** in 136 s — 120 tok/s output |
| output quality | n/a | coherent, correct stop reasons, `glm47` reasoning/tool parsers intact |

Startup shows the Triton binding + backend selection on all 24 workers; KV cache
(`fp8_ds_mla`, 656 B/token layout) sizes as expected.

Note: the runtime validation above ran on this exact diff backported onto v0.28.0 (our
production pin). We are set up to re-validate a main build on the same cluster, and happy to
add unit tests in whatever shape maintainers prefer for device-gated kernels.

### Independent validation on 8× RTX PRO 6000 (SM120, GB202-class)

Separately from the 5090 gang, we ran **GLM-5.2 NVFP4** on a single 8× RTX PRO 6000 (96 GB)
node with this PR's path (`--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla
--reasoning-parser glm47`, `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS`, `VLLM_SPARSE_MLA_SPLITK=32`), TP=8:

| cell (1K in / 256 out) | TP=8 |
|---|---|
| c1 TPOT median | 23.84 ms |
| c1 output tok/s | 36.3 |
| c16 output tok/s | 211.5 |
| KV pool | 480K tok (util 0.90) |

The 433 GB checkpoint fits one node (54.7 GiB weights/GPU at TP=8), serves coherently, and
single-stream decode (23.84 ms) approaches our 24×5090 gang's best (22.8 ms).

**On split-K:** with `VLLM_SPARSE_MLA_SPLITK` unset (the default), c1 TPOT was 44.9 ms;
setting it to 32 dropped it to 23.84 ms — the motivation for the one-time startup hint added
here.

Caveat (same as the 5090 result): this ran as this PR's files overlaid on a v0.28.0 image,
not a clean `main` build — a data point, not CI.

hits.title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Gather the compressed KV once per KV-source group in prefill
hits.body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 keeps compressed KV caches only on its kv-source layers: 2, 8, 14 and 20 on V4.1-Flash. The other 34 compressed layers read their source's cache and never write it.

Before this PR, the mega-attention prefill path (`_forward_prefill_mega`) still dequantized and gathered the whole compressed history into its bf16 workspace in **every** compressed layer:

- Each step made 38 gathers but read only 4 distinct caches.
- On a 16K-token mixed step at 128K context (8 prefills), the gather took ~330 µs per ratio-2 layer and ~655 µs per ratio-1 layer. That is ~19 ms of a 316 ms step, 6% of GPU time.

This PR gathers each source group's compressed history once:

- **Where the gathered data lives:** the gathered chunk sits at the tail of the shared workspace. The scratch of the layers in between is taken from the head, so it does not reach the tail.
- **Consumers:**
  - A consumer checks two things: the span is still intact, and it still holds the same source, step metadata object and chunk.
  - If both hold, the consumer skips the compressed gather and rewrites only its own SWA columns.
- **Source layers** always gather, because they have just inserted this step's rows.
- **`WorkspaceManager.get_retained(key, shape, dtype)`** is new:
  - It returns a view of the last bytes of the scratch workspace, plus a flag saying whether that span is untouched since the previous same-key, same-size call.
  - Any `get_simultaneous` request that reaches into the span clears the flag, as does a reallocation.
  - So the layer gathers again instead of reading stale data, and no memory is added.
- **Sparse indexer:** it now asks for its batch's K gather rows (`max_local_total_seq_lens` over its chunks) instead of the profiled bound `total_seq_lens`.
  - Before, every index layer claimed the whole workspace, which broke the span at L24/28/32/36.
  - The workspace itself is still sized by the profiled bound, so nothing else changes.

## Test Plan

**Serve.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4× B200, TP4 + EP + MegaMoE, DSpark:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1 \
VLLM_DISABLE_DSV4_MEGAMOE_SHARED_EXPERT_FUSION=0 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --served-model-name dsv41 --port 8008 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 512
```

The A/B toggle and the in-server check below come from a test-only copy of the attention file; they are not part of this PR.

- **In-server exactness check.** Every skipped gather was redone into a scratch tensor and compared with the reused columns bitwise, on real 128K-context traffic.

- **Long-context benchmark (`vllm bench serve`).**
  - Warm-up: 64 distinct 126,000-token random prefixes, each sent once with 1 output token to fill the prefix cache.
  - Each measured prompt is one of those prefixes plus a fresh 2,000-token suffix, round-robin over the prefixes.
  - Load: 128,000 input tokens, 1,024 output tokens, concurrency 64, 512 prompts.
  - Arms: the base arm runs the same code with reuse disabled (it gathers in every layer). The two arms ran side by side on one 8× B200 node, one on GPUs 0–3 and the other on GPUs 4–7.

  ```bash
  vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model dsv41 --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
    --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8008 --endpoint /v1/completions \
    --dataset-name custom --dataset-path measure.jsonl --custom-output-len 1024 --skip-chat-template --disable-shuffle \
    --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos --seed 0 --temperature 0 \
    --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
  ```

- **Accuracy.** GSM8K through lm-eval 0.4.12: 5-shot, chat template, thinking off, greedy. Both arms were run.

- **Unit tests.**

  ```bash
  pytest tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py
  ```

## Test Results

**Exactness:**
- 15,400 skipped gathers matched a fresh gather bit for bit, with 0 mismatches.
- Before the indexer change, about 12% of consumer layers still regathered because an index layer had claimed the span (L24/28/32/36). That case always gathers again, so no stale read occurs; the indexer change removes it.

**Memory:** available KV cache memory is 66.3 GiB with this PR, identical to main (38,439,247 tokens). An earlier version with a dedicated buffer cost 4 GiB, because the shared workspace is already sized by the indexer's profiled K gather (5.28 GB).

**Throughput and latency, 128K prefix reuse, concurrency 64:**

These runs predate the indexer change, so the 4 extra gathers per step were still there. The numbers are a lower bound.

| arm | output tok/s | total tok/s | mean TTFT (ms) | p99 TTFT (ms) | p50 ITL (ms) | p99 ITL (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| base | 7,675.1 | 967,059 | 1,150.3 | 3,806.7 | 24.43 | 328.5 |
| this PR | 7,765.7 (+1.2%) | 978,484 (+1.2%) | 956.0 (−16.9%) | 3,695.8 (−2.9%) | 24.44 | 315.2 (−4.1%) |

- A second round with the GPUs swapped is excluded, because its base arm hit a stall.
  - Base arm: 77.4 s duration, p99 TTFT 9.2 s, mean TPOT 7.89 ms. The other three arms were at ~67.5 s, ≤3.8 s and 6.7–7.0 ms.
  - In one 10 s engine-stats window the base arm ran a full batch (64 running, 0 waiting) at 4.3K prompt and 4.3K generation tok/s, against ~11–19K and ~7–10K elsewhere.
  - The cause was not profiled.
- An earlier version with the same reuse logic measured +1.5% and +1.8% output tok/s over two swapped rounds.
- Decode ITL (p50) is unchanged, as expected: the change only touches prefill.

**Scaling:**
- The saved time scales with the compressed history length per prefill request. The rest of a mixed step scales with its new tokens.
- So the gain grows with longer contexts and shorter appends. The 128K context / 2K append above is a middle case.

**Accuracy (GSM8K, 5-shot, 1,319 questions):** identical on both arms.

| arm | exact_match (strict) | exact_match (flexible) |
|---|---:|---:|
| base | 0.7930 ± 0.0112 | 0.9621 ± 0.0053 |
| this PR | 0.7930 ± 0.0112 | 0.9621 ± 0.0053 |

hits.body:
# [Kernel] MXFP4 indexer cache for GLM-5.2 / DSA (glm_moe_dsa)

## What

Adds **MXFP4 (4-bit) support for the DSA lightning-indexer K-cache** and wires it into
GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, `deepseek_v2` `Indexer`). Gated by the existing
`--attention-config '{"use_fp4_indexer_cache": true}'` (default off, behavior unchanged).

Upstream shipped the FP4 indexer **read** path (mqa_logits) for DeepSeek-V4 in #40860, but
the **insert** path is still blocked — `assert not use_fp4_cache, "Unfused FP4 Insert is not
supported yet"` — and `indexer_k_quant_and_cache` is FP8-only. This PR fills that gap.

## Changes (3 files, +122 / −3)

- **`csrc/.../cache_kernels.cu`** (new kernel): `indexer_k_quant_and_cache_mxfp4_kernel`
  writes the indexer K-cache as MXFP4 (E2M1 values + UE8M0 block-32 scales, software E2M1
  encode for sm_100a). Dispatched from `indexer_k_quant_and_cache` when `scale_fmt=="mxfp4"`.
- **`sparse_attn_indexer.py`**: drop the "not supported yet" assert; pass `"mxfp4"` scale_fmt.
- **`deepseek_v2.py`** (`Indexer`): allocate the fp4-shaped K-cache, MXFP4-quantize the
  indexer query, disable the fused FP8 indexer-q path.

## Benefit

Indexer K-cache: **132 → 68 B/token/head (~1.94×)**. Measured on 4×B200 (GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4):

| metric | FP8 indexer | MXFP4 indexer | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPU KV cache size | 1,143,808 tok | 1,184,192 tok | **+3.5%** |
| max concurrency @131K | 8.73× | 9.03× | **+3.4%** |
| TTFT / TPOT (conc1 prefill 8K–122K; conc16 grid; conc48–64 long-ctx) | — | — | neutral |

It's a **memory-efficiency** feature (more KV headroom at long context), not a latency win —
the indexer is a small fraction of prefill vs MLA attention.

## Accuracy

passkey 8K / 32K / 64K = 3/3 · 3/3 · 3/3, identical to FP8. No regression.

## Testing

- Kernel + wiring validated end-to-end on 4×B200 (SM100) serving GLM-5.2-NVFP4: fp4 indexer
  cache active (KV size 1.18M tok), coherent generation, passkey 3/3.
- The `use_fp4_indexer_cache=true` flag was exercised on current-`main` Python (fp4 K-cache
  allocated, 9.09× concurrency). The modified C++ TU (`cache_kernels.cu` = `main` + this diff)
  **compiles clean against `main`'s headers** with CUDA 13.0 / sm_100 (exit 0, no warnings;
  see the compile-verification comment below). Full multi-arch build + link across all TUs is
  still what upstream CI does — a `ready` label would run it.
- Requires SM100 datacenter Blackwell (B200/GB200) — same constraint as the existing
  `use_fp4_indexer_cache` backend assert.

## Notes

- MXFP4 q-quant is done in PyTorch (indexer q is tiny vs attention); a fused q-rope-mxfp4
  kernel could follow.
- GLM's `index_n_heads=32` drives the paged MQA-logits reader at `N=16`; the vendored
  deep_gemm needs `N∈{8,16}` TMEM loaders (a 1-line assert/loader extension, tracked
  separately from this vLLM change).

hits.title: [Bug]: Xid 31 MMU fault under load in multi-node Expert-Parallel (EP16) CUDA-graph replay (fused-MoE FP8 reduce_scatterv) — --enforce-eager clean
hits.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment (click to expand)</summary>

- **vLLM:** `v0.18.0+rhaiv.14` (Red Hat AI build; V1 engine)
- **Model:** `Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-FP8` (MoE, FP8 **block quantization**, `block_n=128`)
- **GPUs:** 2 nodes × 8× **NVIDIA H200** (16 total); NVLink/NVSwitch intra-node, **RoCE** inter-node
- **Parallelism:** `tensor_parallel_size=8`, `data_parallel_size=2`, `enable_expert_parallel=True` (EP16), `data_parallel_size_local=1`
- **Quantization:** `fp8` (block quant); `kv_cache_dtype=auto`
- **all2all manager:** `AgRsAll2AllManager` (default `all2all_backend=allgather_reducescatter`)
- **Attention backend:** `FLASH_ATTN`
- **Compilation (default):** `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`, `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`
- **custom all-reduce:** enabled by default (`disable_custom_all_reduce=False`); crash also occurs with it disabled
- **Serving:** OpenShift AI / KServe `LLMInferenceService` → `LeaderWorkerSet` with `RecreateGroupOnPodRestart` (any worker death tears down + recreates the whole 16-GPU group)

> **EP cannot be disabled for this model.** With `expert=false` the MoE FFN weights get TP8-sharded and the per-shard output size (160) isn't divisible by the FP8 block-quant block (128):
> `ValueError: output_size ... = 160 is not divisible by weight quantization block_n = 128`.
> So EP is mandatory; the only test lever is the EP all-to-all **transport/execution**, not EP on/off.
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Serving **Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-FP8** (MoE) across **2 nodes / 16× H200** (TP8 · DP2 · EP16, RoCE), the engine **crashes with a GPU Xid 31 MMU page fault** within tens of requests under moderate concurrent load.

The fault is **deterministically tied to CUDA-graph-captured execution of the expert-parallel collective path**:

- reproduces with `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` **and** `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`
- **completely disappears with `--enforce-eager`** (cudagraphs off) — 400/400 clean, 16h+ healthy

We have ruled out **hardware**, the **custom all-reduce** kernel, and the **all2all backend choice**. This looks like a cudagraph capture/replay correctness bug in the fused-MoE FP8 + EP `reduce_scatterv` combine path.

#### Reproduction

1. Deploy the model multi-node 16-GPU: TP8 / DP2 / EP16, RoCE, **default** `allgather_reducescatter` backend, cudagraphs **ON** (default).
2. Drive load:
   ```bash
   vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
     --model <name> --dataset-name random \
     --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 0.5 --ignore-eos \
     --max-concurrency 16 --num-prompts 400 --request-rate inf
   ```
3. Within ~30 requests the engine dies; LWS recreates the 16-GPU group (~8 min outage). Also reproduced at `--max-concurrency 8` (crash at the tail of the run). **Halving concurrency does not prevent it** → not a simple capacity/concurrency limit.

Performance is **within SLA right up to the fault** (ITL p50 ~25 ms, TPOT p50 ~34 ms, TTFT p50 ~315 ms) — this is a stability crash, not a saturation/queueing failure.

#### The fault

**GPU driver (authoritative, survives pod recreate) — `dmesg`:**
```text
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:1b:00): 31, pid=..., name=VLLM::Worker, channel 0x0000000c,
  MMU Fault: ENGINE GRAPHICS GPC1 GPCCLIENT_T1_x faulted @ 0x....
  Fault is of type FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ
```
Always on the **rank-0 / TP-0 / EP-0** worker's GPU. Same signature every time (Xid 31, GRAPHICS GPC1, `FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`).

**vLLM traceback (captured live before group recreate) — rank-0 worker (`Worker_DP0_TP0_EP0`).** The illegal access surfaces inside a **PIECEWISE CUDA-graph replay** of the Qwen3 MoE forward, in the **EP combine** collective (condensed; full trace in the collapsible block below):
```text
gpu_model_runner.py:3348 _model_forward
qwen3_moe.py:768 forward
compilation/decorators.py:452 __call__ (aot_compiled_fn)
<eval_with_key>.280:813 forward (submod_70)
compilation/cuda_graph.py:251 __call__
compilation/piecewise_backend.py:377 __call__ (range_entry.runnable)
<inductor graph>  torchinductor_.../c2rna...py:1133 call
torch.ops.vllm.moe_forward.default(buf7, buf8, None, 'from_forward_context')
fused_moe/runner/default_moe_runner.py:85 _moe_forward -> :693 forward_impl
quantization/fp8.py:992 apply -> moe_kernel.apply
fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:1581 apply -> :1381 apply -> :1256 _finalize
fused_moe/prepare_finalize/naive_dp_ep.py:164 finalize
get_ep_group().combine(...)                     # parallel_state.py:1114
cuda_communicator.py:482 combine -> all2all.py:245 combine
dist_group.reduce_scatterv(hidden_states, dim=0, sizes=sizes)
cuda_communicator.py:292 reduce_scatterv
pynccl.py:311 reduce_scatterv -> pynccl_wrapper.py:457 ncclReduce
RuntimeError: NCCL error: unhandled cuda error (run with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO for details)
```
The illegal access then re-raises as `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, which the engine core reports as `EngineDeadError` across all API-server ranks.
On the other API-server/worker ranks the same corruption surfaces downstream as:
```text
Cuda error .../csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:621 'an illegal memory access was encountered'
-> vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError
```
i.e. the MMU fault corrupts the CUDA context on rank-0 (in the EP `reduce_scatterv` combine during graph replay); NCCL then reports "unhandled cuda error" and the custom all-reduce on peers reports the illegal access. **The custom-all-reduce message is a downstream symptom, not the cause** (crash reproduces with custom all-reduce disabled).

#### What we ruled out, and how

| Hypothesis | Experiment | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **Faulty GPU (silicon)** | `dcgmi diag -r 1/3/4` (memtest, pulse, nvbandwidth, pcie, targeted_stress), ECC aggregate, row-remap, NVLink counters on the faulting GPU | **All clean / Pass**, ECC all 0, no row-remap pending |
| **Faulty GPU (silicon)** | Run model **single-node 8-GPU (TP8/EP8)** pinned to each node under identical load | **Both nodes 400/400, 0 Xid** — the "always 1B:00" GPU handled the load cleanly |
| **Faulty GPU (silicon)** | **Leader-swap:** force rank-0 onto the *other* node's GPU0 (different UUID/serial), same load | **Xid 31 moved with rank-0** to the different physical card; old card (now worker) stayed clean → **fault follows the RANK, not the silicon** |
| **Custom all-reduce** | `--disable-custom-all-reduce` (`disable_custom_all_reduce=True` confirmed in engine) | **Still crashes**, identical Xid 31 |
| **EP all2all backend** | `--all2all-backend naive` | Non-viable: worker dies during FULL cudagraph capture (never reaches Ready) |
| **EP all2all backend** | `--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency` | Non-viable: **Xid 43** (kernel launch fail) on all 16 GPUs at KV-cache profiling |
| **CUDA-graph FULL decode graph** | `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` (drop FULL pass) | **Still crashes**, identical Xid 31 |
| **CUDA graphs at all** | `--enforce-eager` (`cudagraph_mode=NONE`) | **400/400 SUCCESS, 0 failed, 0 Xid, engine healthy 16h+** |

**Decisive evidence**

- **Hardware excluded:** fault follows rank-0 across *different physical GPUs* (leader-swap); single-node runs on the "suspect" GPU are 400/400 clean; DCGM / ECC / NVLink all clean.
- **CUDA graphs are the trigger:** the *only* configuration change that eliminates the crash is turning cudagraphs off (`--enforce-eager`). `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` crashes, `PIECEWISE` crashes, `NONE` is clean.
- **Not the custom all-reduce** (crashes on and off) and **not backend math** (eager uses the same kernels and is clean).

#### Suspected root cause

A CUDA-graph capture/replay correctness bug in the **multi-node expert-parallel path** — specifically the fused-MoE FP8 modular kernel combine that performs a variable-size `reduce_scatterv` (`AgRsAll2AllManager.combine` → pynccl `ncclReduce`) inside a piecewise graph. Under concurrent/variable-shape load the replayed graph appears to issue a GPU memory access with a stale/invalid address (MMU `FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ` in the GRAPHICS engine), corrupting the context; NCCL and the custom all-reduce then report secondary errors.

Candidate areas: captured buffers/pointers in the EP combine for dynamic `sizes=`; interaction of `reduce_scatterv` with graph capture; or the FP8 grouped-GEMM MoE path under piecewise inductor partitioning (NCCL collective not honored by `splitting_ops`).

#### Workaround

`--enforce-eager` eliminates the crash but costs throughput/latency:

- eager: **TPOT ~80 ms, ITL ~80 ms, TTFT ~272 ms, ~583 tok/s** @ conc 16 (400/400 clean)
- vs cudagraph single-node: TPOT ~16 ms, ITL ~15 ms

Eager misses our 30–50 ms TPOT target, so it's a functional stopgap, not a performance-acceptable fix. `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` is **not** a usable middle ground (still crashes).

#### Related issues

Not an exact duplicate of any of these, but they form a clear cluster — each matches one axis of this crash:

- **#46253** — *Cross-node piecewise-cudagraph capture → illegal memory access; NCCL collective captured, `splitting_ops` not honored; `--enforce-eager` fixes.* **Closest root-cause thesis.** Differs: theirs faults at **capture** (GB-class, host-staged NCCL); ours faults at **replay** under load on H200 with working RoCE.
- **#58850** — *Intermittent Xid 31 MMU fault in pynccl collective during CUDA graph.* **Closest fault signature** (identical Xid 31 / GRAPHICS GPC / pynccl / CUDA graph). Differs: theirs is intermittent at capture on a TP all-reduce (dense); ours is deterministic at replay in the EP MoE combine.
- **#59189** — *EP serving crashes in NCCL reduce-scatter (EP combine → `reduce_scatterv` → NCCL "unhandled cuda error") under high concurrency.* **Closest stack surface.** Differs: theirs requires `VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=1` (symmetric-memory scratch regression, bisected to #48247) and is **not** cudagraph-triggered; ours is plain pynccl `ncclReduce` and **is** cudagraph-triggered.

**How this report is distinct:** deterministic at **replay under load** (not capture); EP MoE combine via plain pynccl `reduce_scatterv` (not symm-mem); **Xid 31**; `--enforce-eager` clean; on **H200 / RoCE**; both `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` and `PIECEWISE` crash.

#### Questions / asks for triage

- [ ] Is the EP `reduce_scatterv`/all2all combine (`AgRsAll2AllManager`) expected to be CUDA-graph-safe for **variable `sizes=`** across replays? If not, should it be added to `splitting_ops` / excluded from capture for EP?
- [ ] Any known fixes post-`v0.18.0+rhaiv.14` touching fused-MoE modular kernel + cudagraph + EP combine?
- [ ] We can collect `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`, `compute-sanitizer` (memcheck) on rank-0, and a reduced-`cudagraph_capture_sizes` run if helpful — let us know what's most useful.

hits.title: [Elastic EP] Reuse CUDA graphs across reconfiguration
hits.body:
## Summary

[Async preparation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47288) and [eager-mode optimizations](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51885) moved most Elastic EP steps out of the blocking commit path, but CUDA graph mode still blocked serving during kernel warmups and CUDA graph capture on every reconfiguration. This PR removes that work from commit as follows:

1. **Existing ranks reuse their fused-MoE runtime and CUDA graphs.** NIXL EP preserves its graph entries across reconfiguration, while graph-facing tensors and buffers (such as EPLB mapping and dispatch output buffer) keep the same memory addresses.
2. **New ranks warm up and capture during preparation.** Existing ranks keep serving. During new-rank warmup and capture, NIXL EP dispatch and combine mask all remote peers, DP batch coordination is skipped, and FlashInfer tuning results are copied from existing ranks.

CUDA graph reuse is currently only enabled for NIXL EP. Other backends keep the existing recapture path.

**With this PR, we consider Elastic EP reconfiguration downtime solved.**

## Results

We tested full-size `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3` with native FP8 on 24 GB200 GPUs across six nodes, scaling DP/EP `16 -> 24 -> 16` under heavy traffic. The test used vLLM defaults for model length, maximum sequences, and CUDA graph capture. Each revision ran once to warm its torch compile caches and once for measurement on the same allocation. Accuracy passed before and after both reconfigurations.

**Downtime** is the interval in which existing requests do not progress and new requests are rejected.

| Direction | Upstream downtime | This PR | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `16 -> 24` | 40.266 s | **1.019 s** | **97.5%** |
| `24 -> 16` | 38.320 s | **1.895 s** | **95.1%** |

**Total reconfiguration time** covers background preparation and commit.

| Direction | Upstream total | This PR | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `16 -> 24` | 79.571 s | 72.324 s | 9.1% |
| `24 -> 16` | 45.531 s | **9.406 s** | **79.3%** |

## Effect of Max-Capacity Input on Expert Kernel Performance

To keep CUDA graphs stable, the dispatch output buffer is sized for the maximum EP capacity. Padding exists without Elastic EP, but reserving maximum capacity increases the amount of padding. DeepGEMM and FlashInfer CuteDSL avoid padded work and are effectively unaffected. Batched Triton and CUTLASS process more of the padded buffer (for example, Triton does not support masked activations), so Elastic EP amplifies their inefficiency. With active EP fixed at 16, the table compares capacity 64 against capacity 16:

| Expert implementation | Decode throughput change | Prefill throughput change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Batched DeepGEMM | 0.08% higher | 0.97% lower |
| FlashInfer CuteDSL | 1.21% higher | 0.89% lower |
| Batched Triton | 17.58% lower | 13.08% higher |
| Batched CUTLASS FP8 | 77.49% lower | 63.90% lower |

hits.title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Fall back for high-rank MoE LoRA
hits.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55158.

`LoRAConfig` accepts `max_lora_rank` values above 128, but the non-fully-sharded
MoE LoRA dispatch unconditionally selected the one-shot Triton kernel, whose
rank dimension is limited to 128. This caused engine initialization to fail
during CUDA graph warm-up even when the loaded adapter's actual rank was only
4, because the MoE LoRA buffers are padded to the configured maximum rank.

This change:

- keeps ranks up to 128 on the existing one-shot fast path;
- routes larger ranks to the existing two-kernel shrink/expand path;
- lets that fallback preserve the existing `add_inputs=False` contract used by
  dual-stream and other MoE LoRA callers; and
- retains the one-shot assertion as a defensive kernel-local guard.

Rank tiling could extend the one-shot kernel in the future, but the existing
fallback is a smaller correctness-first fix and avoids changing the kernel's
register-pressure/performance characteristics.

## Duplicate check

No exact open issue or fix PR was found after searching for the assertion text,
function name, `max_lora_rank=256`, and MoE LoRA rank fallback. PR #42290's
review did identify both the missing rank fallback and the dual-stream risk,
but those comments were not addressed before merge and current main still has
the mismatch. Related issues and PRs are listed in #55158.

## Test Plan

```bash
uvx --from ruff==0.15.12 ruff format --check \
  vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py \
  tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py

uvx --from ruff==0.15.12 ruff check \
  vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py \
  tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py

uv run --no-sync pytest -q \
  tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py \
  -k large_rank_fallback
```

The targeted numerical test compares the Triton result with a PyTorch
reference across:

- rank 128 (one-shot boundary) and 256 (fallback);
- `add_inputs=True` and `False`; and
- one and two LoRA slices, covering both TMA descriptor layouts on supported
  GPUs.

An end-to-end check starts the public Nemotron MoE model from #55158 with
`--max-lora-rank 256` and verifies that CUDA graph warm-up completes and a LoRA
request returns HTTP 200.

## Test Result

- Ruff format: passed.
- Ruff lint: passed.
- Python syntax and custom-op real/fake signature checks: passed.
- Targeted numerical test on an NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB: passed
  (`8 passed, 417 deselected`). This covers rank 128/256,
  `add_inputs=True/False`, and one/two LoRA slices.
- End-to-end test on 2x NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB with TP=2: passed. At commit
  `29a6af589`, the public Nemotron MoE model and rank-4 dummy adapter started
  with `--max-lora-rank 256`; both PIECEWISE and FULL CUDA graph capture
  completed, `/health` returned HTTP 200, and a request to the `dummy` LoRA
  model returned HTTP 200.

GPU test environment: PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA runtime 13.0, compute
capability 8.0.

## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex assisted with code-path analysis, drafting the patch and tests,
and duplicate-work research. The human submitter reviewed every changed line,
validated the design, and verified the reported GPU test results.
