hits.title: [Bug]: MoE LoRA one-shot path rejects max_lora_rank=256 although LoRAConfig accepts it
hits.body:
## Environment

- vLLM: `0.28.1rc1.dev344+ge6eb9074e`
- vLLM commit: `e6eb9074e9f1fce6115dc036b40d07ebaa926979`
- The relevant config, dispatch, and assertion are unchanged on current main
  `bb363db9a5ec2edc7b39e99b00af363a89d1fb81` as of 2026-09-03. The full
  end-to-end reproduction below was run on `e6eb9074e`.
- GPU: `2 x NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB`
- Base model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16`
  - revision: `bf77c3174f68ad409e1c2aa60daeb46e32d1c606`
- Adapter: `ace-nguyen/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16-dummy-moe-lora`
  - revision: `c7a2f3395ad0d9612edaa9ff6a2975a4a8bab921`
  - actual adapter rank: `4`

## Reproduction

Run the same public model and adapter twice, changing only
`--max-lora-rank`.

### Control: rank 128

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve \
  nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-lora \
  --lora-modules \
    dummy=ace-nguyen/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16-dummy-moe-lora \
  --max-lora-rank 128 \
  --max-model-len 2048 \
  --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \
  --trust-remote-code
```

After the server becomes ready, send a short LoRA request:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "dummy",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly OK."}],
    "temperature": 0,
    "max_completion_tokens": 8
  }'
```

Observed control result: the server starts, logs `Using fused MoE LoRA
implementation`, and the LoRA request returns HTTP 200.

### Failing case: rank 256

Stop the control server and run the same command with only this change:

```diff
-  --max-lora-rank 128 \
+  --max-lora-rank 256 \
```

The engine fails during initialization/warm-up, before the API server becomes
ready:

```text
AssertionError: fused_moe_lora_one_shot supports max_lora_rank<=128; got rank=256
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'fused_moe_lora_one_shot supports max_lora_rank<=128; got rank=256'
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
```

Both tensor-parallel workers hit the same assertion.

## Observed behavior

`LoRAConfig` accepts `max_lora_rank=256`, but the selected non-fully-sharded
fused MoE-LoRA one-shot path rejects the padded maximum rank during engine
warm-up. This makes the entire server fail to start even though the loaded
adapter's actual rank is only 4.

## Expected behavior

One of the following should happen:

1. Ranks greater than 128 are routed to a compatible fallback implementation;
2. the one-shot implementation tiles the rank dimension; or
3. vLLM rejects this model/path/configuration combination before model loading
   with an intentional, actionable `ValueError`.

An accepted global LoRA configuration should not reach a raw assertion after
the model weights have been loaded.

## Why this is inconsistent

`LoRAConfig.MaxLoRARanks` includes `256`, `320`, and `512`:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e6eb9074e9f1fce6115dc036b40d07ebaa926979/vllm/config/lora.py#L27-L35

For non-fully-sharded MoE LoRA, dispatch reaches the one-shot implementation
without a `max_lora_rank > 128` fallback:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e6eb9074e9f1fce6115dc036b40d07ebaa926979/vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py#L1479-L1524

The one-shot wrapper then asserts that the rank is at most 128:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e6eb9074e9f1fce6115dc036b40d07ebaa926979/vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py#L345-L354

The source comment explains the kernel-local restriction, but this restriction
is not reflected in validation or dispatch.

## Suggested fix direction

- Route ranks greater than 128 to the existing shrink/expand path, including
  its `add_inputs=False` callers.
- Alternatively, add a model/path-aware initialization check before loading
  model weights.
- Longer term, implement rank tiling in the one-shot kernel.

A regression test should cover the boundary:

- rank 128 continues to use the one-shot path;
- rank 256 either completes through a supported fallback or fails early with
  an intentional validation error;
- cover normal and dual-stream MoE-LoRA dispatch if both use this path.

## Related, but not duplicates

- PR #42290 introduced the one-shot MoE-LoRA kernel. Review comments already
  noted that rank greater than 128 should fall back to the legacy path and that
  dual-stream dispatch needed the same guard, but the merged implementation
  still asserts:
  - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42290#discussion_r3216969192
  - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42290#discussion_r3216969204
- Issue #40038 uses the same model and dummy adapter on A100, but reports a
  mixed base/LoRA batch metadata OOB after startup. It was fixed by #40131 and
  is distinct from this rank-dependent startup assertion:
  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40038
- Issue #3934 is an older, closed general LoRA rank request and does not track
  the current fused MoE one-shot dispatch behavior:
  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/3934
- PR #44147 is a FlashInfer MoE-LoRA backend and its public tests do not cover
  rank 256:
  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44147

No exact open issue or fix PR was found as of 2026-09-03.

## Workaround

If all loaded adapters have actual rank at most 128, configure
`--max-lora-rank 128` (or lower). `--fully-sharded-loras` may bypass the
one-shot path when expert parallelism is disabled, but it has not been
validated with this reproduction and is not compatible with expert parallelism.

hits.title: [ModelOpt] Support fused MoE weight reload
hits.body:
## Purpose

Refs #53687.

The native MoE checkpoint loader currently reaches fused ModelOpt NVFP4 parameters through per-expert, per-projection checkpoint records. For the Qwen3-30B-A3B example in #53687, that requires:

```text
42 layers * 128 experts * 3 projections * 4 tensor kinds = 64,512 records
```

This PR adds an opt-in, layer-fused loading contract so an online quantizer can instead provide the eight complete pre-kernel tensors owned by each `RoutedExperts` layer:

- `w13_{weight,weight_scale,weight_scale_2,input_scale}`
- `w2_{weight,weight_scale,weight_scale_2,input_scale}`

That reduces the example above to `42 * 8 = 336` loader records without bypassing vLLM's reload lifecycle.

Specifically, this PR:

- adds `FusedMoEParameterLoadSpec`, through which a quantization method declares each accepted checkpoint name, destination parameter, exact shape, dtype, sharding, and scale domain;
- makes the default contract empty, so existing quantization methods retain the current per-expert path;
- opts ModelOpt NVFP4 into the contract for its eight layer-local tensors;
- copies complete tensors directly into their existing parameter storage;
- rejects duplicate, incomplete, mixed-granularity, shape-mismatched, and dtype-mismatched bundles;
- keeps normal layerwise accounting and post-load processing intact.

The fused input must already match the destination layout declared by the layer on the current rank. TP, EP, EPLB, padding, and backend-specific layout decisions remain vLLM responsibilities. The legacy expert-name mapping remains the fallback and is built lazily only when that path is used.

This does not duplicate an existing PR. Searches for #53687 and for fused MoE reload support found no open implementation; the issue also had no linked PR when this work started.

No documentation update is required because this is an internal weight-loader contract and adds no user-facing option or supported model architecture.

## Test Plan

Run the fused and legacy MoE loader regression suite:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py \
  -v
```

Run the focused layerwise reload lifecycle regression:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py::test_layer_fused_reload_uses_normal_processing_and_preserves_storage \
  -v
```

Run a native ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE kernel correctness case on SM120:

```bash
VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  'tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py::test_moe_layer_no_parallel[False-False-False-modelopt_fp4-2-8-1-128-256]' \
  -v -s
```

Run the relevant static checks:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-check --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/__init__.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe_method_base.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/__init__.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe_method_base.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py

git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

The tests cover complete fused bundles, exact destination copies, duplicate and incomplete bundles, mixed fused/legacy input in both orders, shape and dtype contract violations, ModelOpt NVFP4 metadata, legacy loading behavior, layerwise completeness accounting, post-load processing, parameter storage identity, and a native NVFP4 MoE kernel invocation.

## Test Result

Validation was run on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, driver 580.173.02), with Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132, and CUDA 13.2:

- MoE loader regression suite: `53 passed, 14 warnings in 14.96s`.
- Layerwise fused reload lifecycle regression: `1 passed, 14 warnings in 0.64s`.
- Native ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE kernel case: `1 passed, 14 warnings in 3.22s`.

The native kernel test selected `VLLM_CUTLASS` on SM120, rather than an emulation backend, and matched the reference output within the test's ModelOpt FP4 tolerance.

### Qwen3-30B-A3B loader-only benchmark

A controlled temporary benchmark used the issue's Qwen3-30B-A3B routed-expert dimensions: 42 layers, 128 experts, hidden size 2048, intermediate size 768, TP=1, EP=1, and EPLB disabled. Both paths loaded the same eight synthetic, shape- and dtype-correct GPU-resident source tensors and copied the same 339,741,696 bytes per layer. Each sample timed exactly 42 sequential `RoutedExperts.load_weights` calls, with `torch.cuda.synchronize()` immediately before and after the measured region. One warm-up was followed by five paired samples in alternating order.

| Path | Loader records | Mean | Median | Observed range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Legacy per-expert | 64,512 | 5.3220 s | 5.3175 s | 5.3140-5.3410 s |
| Layer-fused | 336 | 19.928 ms | 19.929 ms | 19.924-19.933 ms |

This is a 267.1x mean and 266.8x median speedup for the isolated loader boundary. Before timing, all eight pre-kernel destination tensors loaded through the fused and legacy paths were required to be exactly equal. After timing, both layers ran the real ModelOpt NVFP4 post-load conversion and `VLLM_CUTLASS` forward path; their processed parameters and outputs were also exactly equal (`rtol=0`, `atol=0`), and the outputs were finite.

This benchmark intentionally measures only Python loader granularity plus the identical GPU copy volume. It excludes online quantization, IPC or weight transfer, layerwise finalization, post-load conversion time, and model-level reload orchestration. The 267x figure is therefore not an end-to-end `reload_weights` claim.

Additional validation:

- Fused destination tensors exactly matched their supplied inputs, while the existing legacy loader coverage remained passing.
- The reload lifecycle test invoked post-load processing exactly once and preserved both the original `Parameter` objects and their storage pointers.
- `ruff-check`: passed.
- Python 3.12 `mypy`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Before this change, ModelOpt NVFP4 online-quantized MoE weights had to be expanded into per-expert checkpoint names. With this contract, the workload described in #53687 can present 336 complete layer-local records instead of 64,512 records, a roughly 99.5% reduction in Python loader applications.

The 90-step GB200 production benchmark reported in #53687 measured mean refit time decreasing from 18.42 seconds to 6.31 seconds (2.92x) with a downstream proof of concept. That GB200 benchmark was not rerun as part of this PR. SM120 and GB200 use different architectures, and the measurement boundaries differ, so the loader-only result above is not presented as a reproduction of that end-to-end result.

No model evaluation was run because this change does not alter quantization arithmetic, kernel selection, or model computation. It changes loader granularity while preserving exact pre-kernel tensor values and the existing post-load processing path.

## AI Assistance


---

<details>
<summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR and the issue it addresses.
- [x] The test commands that were run.
- [x] The test results and the relevant before/after loader comparison.
- [x] Documentation impact was evaluated; no update is required.
- [ ] The human submitter reviewed every changed line and can defend the change end to end.

</details>

hits.title: [Bug]: CPU MXFP4 MoE (gpt-oss) broken on AMD EPYC after AMX gate
hits.body:
## Summary

Serving native MXFP4 `gpt-oss` (e.g. `RedHatAI/gpt-oss-120b`) on **AMD EPYC (Zen)** fails on **vLLM 0.28+** after `#50801` gated `CPUExpertsMxfp4` on Intel AMX (`torch.cpu._is_amx_tile_supported()`). No EPYC CPU has AMX. The MXFP4 oracle still selects `Mxfp4MoeBackend.CPU` on CPU hosts, then the AMX gate rejects the deployment.

```text
ValueError: Mxfp4 MoE backend 'CPU' does not support the deployment configuration since kernel does not support current device cpu.
```

`ZenCpuPlatform` / zentorch still activate on these hosts; they do not change MXFP4 MoE selection. This is a **regression** introduced by the AMX gate: prior to `#50801`, `CPUExpertsMxfp4._supports_current_device()` was `is_cpu()` only.

## Environment

- **vLLM:** `0.28.0`
- **Model:** `RedHatAI/gpt-oss-120b` (`quantization=gpt_oss_mxfp4`)
- **Hardware:** AMD EPYC (Zen), AVX-512
- **Platform log:** `AMD Zen CPU detected with zentorch installed, using ZenCpuPlatform`
- **Device:** `device_config=cpu`

Upstream tags:
- Through **0.27.x**: `CPUExpertsMxfp4` gated on `is_cpu()` only
- From **`v0.28.0rc1` / `v0.28.0`**: AMX-gated

## Regression introduced by

- **PR:** https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50801 — `[CPU] Refine CPU kernel dispatch`
- **Merged:** 2026-08-03 (`c8602c79`)
- **Shipped in:** v0.28.0 line
- **File:** `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/cpu_moe.py`

```diff
-        return current_platform.is_cpu()
+        return (
+            current_platform.is_cpu()
+            and current_platform.get_cpu_architecture() == CpuArchEnum.X86
+            and torch.cpu._is_amx_tile_supported()
+        )
```

Related: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41922 added CPU MXFP4 MoE with the previous `is_cpu()` gate. After `#50801`, CPU MXFP4 MoE is effectively **Intel-AMX-only**, with no non-AMX CPU fallback in `oracle/mxfp4.py`.

## Logs (failing — 0.28 on AMD EPYC)

```text
INFO ... AMD Zen CPU detected with zentorch installed, using ZenCpuPlatform.
INFO ... Triton is installed but 0 active driver(s) found (expected 1). Disabling Triton ...
(APIServer pid=1) ... version 0.28.0
(APIServer pid=1) ... model   RedHatAI/gpt-oss-120b
(APIServer pid=1) non-default args: {..., 'model': 'RedHatAI/gpt-oss-120b', 'max_model_len': 131072, ...}
(EngineCore ...) ... quantization=gpt_oss_mxfp4 ... device_config=cpu ...
(Worker pid=...) INFO ... Starting to load model RedHatAI/gpt-oss-120b...
(Worker pid=...) INFO ... [mxfp4.py:539] Using 'CPU' Mxfp4 MoE backend.
(Worker pid=...) ERROR ... WorkerProc failed to start.
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py", line 147, in __init__
    self.mxfp4_backend, self.experts_cls = select_mxfp4_moe_backend(moe)
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py", line 540, in select_mxfp4_moe_backend
    return _return_or_raise(
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py", line 423, in _return_or_raise
    raise ValueError(_make_log_unsupported(backend, reason))
ValueError: Mxfp4 MoE backend 'CPU' does not support the deployment configuration since kernel does not support current device cpu.
```

Gate applied in 0.28:

```python
def _supports_current_device() -> bool:
    return (
        current_platform.is_cpu()
        and current_platform.get_cpu_architecture() == CpuArchEnum.X86
        and torch.cpu._is_amx_tile_supported()   # false on EPYC
    )
```

## Requested fix

Add support for MXFP4 MoE on AMD Zen / EPYC CPU (non-AMX), so native gpt-oss MXFP4 checkpoints can run under `ZenCpuPlatform` on 0.28+.

hits.title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoE] Fix AITER MoE routing fallback to eager torch.topk for scoring_func=softmax
hits.body:
## Purpose

MoE token routing in `fused_topk_bias()` falls back to the slow, unfused eager `torch.topk` path whenever AITER MoE fusion is enabled (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1`) and `scoring_func != "sigmoid"`.

**Root cause:** the routing dispatch only had a fused fast path for `scoring_func == "sigmoid"` (via `rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk`) and `"sqrtsoftplus"` (via `dsv4_topk`). Any other case -- notably `"softmax"`, used by classic/DeepSeek-V3-style MoE routing -- falls through every dispatch branch to a fully eager PyTorch implementation (`softmax()` + `torch.topk()` + `.gather()`), even though vLLM already ships a fused `vllm_topk_softmax` kernel for this exact case (already used on the non-AITER path).


**Fix:** add an explicit dispatch branch for `scoring_func == "softmax"` that routes to the existing fused `vllm_topk_softmax` kernel before falling through to the eager path. This is a routing-logic fix only,  no new kernel code, just correcting which existing, already-tested kernel gets called.

**Known follow-up (out of scope here):** `scoring_func == "sigmoid"` with `topk < num_expert_group` still falls through to the eager path both before and after this fix; left untouched to keep this PR minimal.

## Test Plan

Added `test_fused_topk_bias_softmax_dispatches_to_fused_kernel_under_aiter` in `tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py`, which mocks `rocm_aiter_ops.is_fused_moe_enabled() == True` and asserts `vllm_topk_softmax` is called (not eager `torch.topk`) for
`scoring_func="softmax"`.

## Test Result

Full test suite on real MI350 (gfx950) hardware: **721 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, including the new regression test above.

Direct microbenchmark (`num_tokens=4096, hidden_size=8192, num_experts=128, topk=8`, bf16, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1`):

| Path | Latency |
|---|---|
| eager `torch.topk` (before fix) | 0.0546 ms/call |
| fused `vllm_topk_softmax` (after fix) | 0.0130 ms/call |

**4.19x speedup** on the routing call itself.

---

hits.title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix channelwise GPTQ MoE fallback
hits.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52715.

On ROCm, AutoGPTQ MoE layers that cannot use GPTQMoeMarlin fall back to the Triton WNA16 backend. For channel-wise GPTQ checkpoints, `group_size=-1` was incorrectly used in tensor-size arithmetic, causing `RuntimeError: zeros: Dimension size must be non-negative` during weight allocation. This PR allocates one scale/zero-point group per output channel and resolves `-1` to the current GEMM's K dimension at launch time, which correctly handles the different K dimensions of w13 and w2. Existing positive group-size paths are unchanged.

I checked issue #52715, its comments, open PRs referencing the issue, and open PRs matching the ROCm GPTQ MoE/channel-wise keywords. No open PR currently addresses this issue. PR #52716 was closed without merging because changing allocation shapes alone would leave negative scale offsets in the Triton kernel; this implementation fixes both allocation and runtime scale indexing.

## Test Plan

Run the allocation regression tests and the channel-wise Triton numerical correctness tests:

```bash
uv run --active --no-sync .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_moe_wna16.py 'tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py::test_wna16_triton_channelwise_group_size' -q
```

Run offline inference on an AMD Radeon 8060S (`gfx1151`) with `TheBloke/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-GPTQ` (`GPTQ INT4`, `group_size=-1`, `desc_act=true`):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/home/tang/vllm VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=WARNING uv run --active --no-sync .venv/bin/python build/offline_mixtral_gptq.py --prompt "What is the capital of France? Answer in one complete sentence." --max-tokens 32
```

## Test Result

Before this change, the model failed before inference while creating MoE scale tensors:

```text
Layer 'model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.experts' is not supported by GPTQMoeMarlin. Falling back to Moe WNA16 kernels.
Using 'TRITON' WNA16 MoE backend.
RuntimeError: zeros: Dimension size must be non-negative
```

After this change, the targeted tests pass:

```text
18 passed, 9 skipped
ruff check: passed
ruff format: passed
```

The model loaded all 22.18 GiB of weights, selected `TritonWNA16Experts`, executed `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq`, and completed offline inference.

Input:

```text
What is the capital of France? Answer in one complete sentence.
```

Output:

```text
The capital of France is Paris, a global center for art, fashion, gastronomy and culture, situated on the Seine River in the north of the country
```

hits.title: [MoE] Optimize fused MoE token alignment and adaptive block size for fine-grained experts
hits.body:
## Summary

Fine-grained Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures with high expert counts (such as Gemma 4 26B-A4B with E=128, top-k=8) experience severe fixed kernel launch overhead and padding inflation in vLLM's Triton fused MoE path during small-batch decode (M <= 4).

This PR introduces dynamic token alignment bypass when expert token collision is negligible (`M * topk * 4 <= E`), clamps naive block size to 16, and provides adaptive default tile sizing for fine-grained MoEs (E >= 128). Tested on upstream HEAD with an 8x NVIDIA H100 platform, this achieves up to a **1.50x speedup** on small-batch MoE dispatches (saving 35-46 µs per dispatch, ~1.05-1.38 ms per generated decode token across 30 layers) with zero loss in numerical accuracy.

---

## Purpose

- **Problem Statement**:
  1. **Fixed Kernel Launch Overhead**: In vLLM's Triton fused MoE implementation, `ops.moe_align_block_size` incurs a fixed ~20-27 µs CUDA kernel launch and prefix-sum latency per dispatch. Across the two GEMM dispatches (W13 and W2) in 30 decoder layers, this accounts for ~1.2-1.6 ms of invariant latency per generated decode token.
  2. **Padding Inflation**: The default `BLOCK_SIZE_M = 64` pads token-to-expert assignments up to multiples of 64. At M=1 (8 active tokens for top-k=8), this produces 512 padded tokens—a **64.00x padding overhead** where **98.4% of processed rows are dummy padding**.
  3. **Sorting Redundancy at Low Sparsity**: When `(M * topk) / E <= 0.25` (i.e. `M * topk * 4 <= E`), tokens are so sparsely distributed across experts that token collision on any individual expert is near zero (<= 1 token per expert). Under this regime, sorting and grouping tokens yields zero packing benefit while paying the full 20-27 µs alignment latency penalty.

- **Changes Made**:
  1. **Dynamic Token Alignment Bypass** (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py`):
     - Dynamically evaluates `M * topk * 4 <= E` per forward pass.
     - When satisfied, sets `sorted_token_ids=None` to engage Triton's naive block assignment path, bypassing `ops.moe_align_block_size` entirely.
     - Enforces `BLOCK_SIZE_M = min(config.get("BLOCK_SIZE_M", 16), 16)` in naive mode to prevent redundant computation over dummy padding rows.
     - Adds full support for `expert_map` in the naive path via `expert_map[topk_ids.view(-1)]`.
     - Guards against quantized WNA16 formats which do not support naive assignment.
     - Routes `TritonWNA16Experts.forward()` through `_prepare_expert_assignment` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py`).
  2. **Adaptive Default Tile Sizes for Fine-Grained MoEs (E >= 128)**:
     - In `get_default_config()`, sets `BLOCK_SIZE_M` adaptively based on batch size: M <= 64 -> 16, M <= 256 -> 32, M > 256 -> 64.
     - Corrects the `tokens_per_expert` calculation to include top-k: `(M * topk) // max(E, 1)`.
  3. **Backwards-Compatible `moe_sum` Dispatcher** (`vllm/_custom_ops.py`):
     - Added dual 2-arg / 4-arg fallback to support differing C++ extension build signatures seamlessly.
  4. **Documentation**:
     - Internal kernel execution optimization; no public API changes or user-facing doc updates required.

---

## Test Plan

The following test suite verifies functional correctness, bit-for-bit numerical equivalence, regression freedom across existing alignment pathways, and end-to-end model generation:

1. **Unit Tests (Fine-Grained MoE & Crossover Logic)**:
   ```bash
   pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_moe_fine_grained.py
   ```
   Verifies:
   - Bit-for-bit numerical equivalence (`atol=0.0`) between naive bypass and aligned path.
   - Crossover boundary switching behavior from naive (M=4) to aligned (M=5) for E=128, top-k=8.
   - Dynamic block size selection and clamping behavior.
   - Custom `expert_map` index mapping in naive mode.

2. **Regression Suite (Existing MoE Alignment)**:
   ```bash
   pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_align_block_size.py
   ```

3. **Code Quality & Linters**:
   ```bash
   ruff check vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/ tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_moe_fine_grained.py vllm/_custom_ops.py
   ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/ tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_moe_fine_grained.py vllm/_custom_ops.py
   ```

4. **Kernel & Model Benchmarks**:
   ```bash
   # Crossover boundary benchmark across batch sizes
   python scratch/crossover_benchmark.py

   # End-to-end model generation benchmarks
   python scratch/benchmark_generation_moe_models.py
   ```

---

## Test Result

All tests and benchmarks were executed on an 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (SXM5) platform on current upstream HEAD.

### 1. Unit Test Results
- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_moe_fine_grained.py`: **12 passed in 13.61s**.
- `ruff check` & `ruff format --check`: **All checks passed; clean formatting**.

### 2. Isolated Kernel Benchmark (E=128, top-k=8, H=2816, N=704)
| Batch Size (M) | Aligned Path (µs) | Naive Path (µs) | Time Saved (µs) | Speedup | Winner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **M = 1** (Decode) | 130.73 | **95.66** | **35.07** | **1.37x** | **NAIVE** |
| **M = 2** | 137.71 | **91.63** | **46.08** | **1.50x** | **NAIVE** |
| **M = 3** | 127.38 | **113.76** | **13.62** | **1.12x** | **NAIVE** |
| **M = 4** | 135.99 | 142.83 | -6.85 | 0.95x | ALIGNED |
| **M = 8** | 239.02 | 260.41 | -21.40 | 0.92x | ALIGNED |

- Saving 35.07 µs to 46.08 µs per dispatch translates to **~1.05 ms to 1.38 ms saved per generated decode token** across 30 decoder layers.
- **Numerical Parity**: `max |y_naive - y_aligned| = 0.000000` confirms bit-for-bit numerical equivalence.

### 3. End-to-End Model Generation Benchmarks
Tested with real pre-trained MoE models under greedy generation (64 output tokens per request):

- **OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct** (E=64, top-k=8):
  - Batch Size 1 (naive bypass): **12.85 ms/token** (77.8 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 2 (naive bypass): **13.02 ms/token** (153.7 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 4 (aligned path): **13.59 ms/token** (294.3 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 8 (aligned path): **13.74 ms/token** (582.4 tok/s)

- **Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat** (E=60, top-k=4):
  - Batch Size 1 (naive bypass): **24.00 ms/token** (41.7 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 2 (naive bypass): **25.74 ms/token** (77.7 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 4 (aligned path): **27.73 ms/token** (144.3 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 8 (aligned path): **27.87 ms/token** (287.1 tok/s)

- **Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it** (E=128, top-k=8):
  - Batch Size 1 (naive bypass): **36.10 ms/token** (27.7 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 2 (naive bypass): **36.06 ms/token** (55.5 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 4 (aligned path): **39.70 ms/token** (100.8 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 8 (aligned path): **38.58 ms/token** (207.4 tok/s)

- **Text Quality**: All generated samples match expected greedy outputs with zero degradation or token corruption.

---

## Duplicate-Work Check

Prior to opening this PR, the following searches were executed against upstream `vllm-project/vllm`:
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "moe token alignment"`
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "moe_align_block_size in:body"`

**Findings**: Existing open PRs touching MoE token alignment are ROCm-specific (#51515) or address deep EP / Marlin fusing (#53911, #44167). No existing PR implements dynamic alignment bypass for sparse regimes or fine-grained MoE tile size clamping for 128+ experts.

---

## Statement of AI Assistance

This pull request was prepared with AI assistance (Jetski pair programmer) and reviewed, benchmarked, and verified by Douglas Reid.

hits.title: [Test Coverage] Add tests for MoE dispatch and Triton qzeros reshape
hits.body:
## Purpose

Two dispatch/format-layer gaps in the WNA16 MoE path, plus a one-line diagnostic fix a test exposed.

**1. `CompressedTensorsMoEMethod.get_moe_method` had no direct test coverage.** It is pure routing logic — given a quantization scheme (plus platform/config state on the ROCm branches) it picks one of ~9 backend MoE method classes. The ROCm selection hinges on a 7-term `AND` (native RDNA kernel vs. gfx950 FlyDSL vs. emulation fallback); a single dropped term silently misroutes production traffic. An unreachable-branch bug (dead `CompressedTensorsW4A16FlydslMoEMethod` path, indentation) already shipped this way in #44570 and sat unnoticed for weeks — [#44570 (comment)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44570#discussion_r3440228634). `test_flydsl_moe.py` exercises the kernel, not the dispatch.

**2. The Triton qzeros reshape in `convert_to_wna16_moe_kernel_format` had no regression coverage.** AutoGPTQ / compressed-tensors checkpoints persist packed weights K-first int32; the `TRITON` branch transposes w13/w2 and scales into the N-first packed-uint8 layout `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` expects. The zero-point transpose was missing until #52112 added it (chasing an unrelated bug, no reference to #44570 or its review thread), and it shipped with no test. A byte/nibble permutation there does not crash — it silently offsets every dequantized weight.

**3. Diagnostic fix (1 line).** While adding an invalid-format case, the `ValueError` in that branch was found to print the *required* format constant instead of the *received* `format` — `f"but got format: {CompressionFormat.pack_quantized.value}"` → `f"but got format: {format}"`. No behavior change: the raise already happened for these configs; only its wording changes. `test_wna16_invalid_bits_or_format_raises[bad-format]` now locks it in.

### Files

| file | contents |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_moe_dispatch.py` | 28 tests — scheme resolution, simple + weight/input backend routing, NVFP4 routing, and the three ROCm sub-branches of the wNa16 path, including a parametrized check that the gfx950/FlyDSL 7-term `AND` requires every term individually. Every backend class is mocked → asserts routing only (which class, which args), no GPU/model dependency. |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_wna16_moe_triton_gptq_qzeros.py` | 4 tests — the K-first int32 → N-first uint8 qzeros transform maps each channel's zero-point to the exact byte/nibble `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` reads (`out[e, bn // 2, kg]`), verified against an independently constructed reference; plus the `qzeros=None` (symmetric-checkpoint) path. Parametrized over `AutoGPTQConfig` (sym) and `QuantizationArgs` (asym — where the zero-point values are load-bearing). Pure tensor-shape/value test, no kernel launch. |
| `compressed_tensors_moe.py` | the 1-line message fix above. |

Each test file lives in the tree of the implementation it exercises so it rides that impl's Buildkite `source_file_dependencies` — dispatch (`layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/`) → `kernels-quantization-test`; qzeros (`layers/fused_moe/oracle/int_wna16.py`) → `kernels-moe-test` — per [#53643 review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53643).

### Not a duplicate

`get_moe_method` has no dispatch-layer tests on `main`; #52112 shipped the qzeros transpose with none; no open PR adds either. This traces to two acknowledged-but-unfixed threads from #44570 ([dispatch coverage](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44570#discussion_r3440228634), [qzeros](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44570)). Related: #52112 (the qzeros fix this covers), RFC #53629 (streaming-time weight conversion, spun out of this work).

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_moe_dispatch.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_wna16_moe_triton_gptq_qzeros.py -q
```

Both are CPU-only (all backends mocked / no kernel launch). Regression check for the diagnostic fix: revert the `compressed_tensors_moe.py` line and confirm `test_wna16_invalid_bits_or_format_raises[bad-format]` / `[both-bad]` fail while `[bad-bits]` still passes.

## Test Result

Python 3.12, CPU:

```
tests/kernels/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_moe_dispatch.py .... 28 passed
tests/kernels/moe/test_wna16_moe_triton_gptq_qzeros.py ..............   4 passed
```

Regression check: with the `compressed_tensors_moe.py` line reverted, `[bad-format]` and `[both-bad]` fail (`assert "got format: naive-quantized" in ...` — message still said `pack-quantized`), `[bad-bits]` passes. With the fix, all 3 pass.

No model evaluation: the only non-test change is the text of a `ValueError` raised at load time for an already-invalid config — it cannot affect routing, model output, accuracy, or serving.

AI assistance (Claude) was used; I have reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.

hits.title: [Bugfix][Hardware][AMD] Handle AITER unified-attention LDS overflow with Triton fallback
hits.body:
## Purpose On ROCm, AITER's `kernel_unified_attention_3d` can request more LDS than the GPU provides. On affected Wave32 archs, `select_3d_config` chooses a tile size and pipeline depth **without checking the LDS budget**, so once Triton double-buffers the K/V tiles, the kernel asks for **65792** bytes against the 65536-byte (64 KB) limit. Triton raises an `OutOfResources` error in its pre-launch shared-memory check at the first 3D-kernel launch (during CUDA-graph capture in the default path) which aborts server startup. Since the root-cause is with AITER's select_3d_config call, this bugfix adds a one-shot, defensive fallback in the ROCm AITER unified-attention backend. It catches the first LDS-overflow error from the causal AITER launch, logs a warning once, latches a per-instance flag, and routes that and every later causal forward to the in-tree `triton_unified_attention` kernel for the rest of the process. The error is then recognized by a typed check against `triton.runtime.errors.OutOfResources` with a message-text fallback, so it survives Triton refactors. The non-causal path already used the in-tree kernel; that call site is extracted into a shared `_forward_triton_unified` helper so no attention logic is duplicated. Triton's `OutOfResources` is a pure pre-launch Python check, so no GPU work is enqueued. The fallback is safe inside CUDA-graph capture (verified bit-identical to eager). This is a vLLM-side stopgap; the underlying tile/LDS budgeting belongs in AITER's `select_3d_config` I have tracked it upstream at ROCm/aiter#4329. Not a duplicate: #48723 is open and unassigned, and the AGENTS.md duplicate-work checks (`gh issue view 48723`, `gh pr list --search "48723 in:body"`, `gh pr list --search "aiter unified attention LDS"`) returned no PR addressing this, which I verified immediately before opening. Catching `OutOfResources` from a Triton launch and rerouting at runtime is an established in-tree idiom: `vllm/triton_utils/force_first_config.py` (imports it at line 31, catches at line 67) and `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py` (at line 1257) both do it. The only difference here is that those pick a different config of the same kernel; this picks a different kernel.
